title: Enhanced respiratory syncytial virus surveillance of young children admitted to the Sydney Children’s Hospitals Network, 2019–2023
abstract: OBJECTIVES: In this study, we aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network (SCHN), determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission. STUDY TYPE: Multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years. METHODS: The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. Participants were children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023, comprising all ICU admitted, and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients. The main outcome measures were characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years. RESULTS: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001). Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission in multivariate logistic regression were decreasing month of age (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.11), prematurity (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.61-2.91), Indigenous identity (OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.30-7.56) and cardiac disease (OR 3.39, 95% CI 2.06-5.70). The average hospitalisation incidence rate was 1615 per 100,000 (95% CI 1565-1666), with higher rates among children aged <1 year, 2141 per 100,000 (95% CI 2061-2224) compared with those aged 1-2 years, 1088 per 100,000 (95% CI 1030-1148). CONCLUSIONS: RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life. Children who are Indigenous, were born prematurely or have heart disease are at greatest risk of severe disease and may benefit from extended preventative programs.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, involving 4414 children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, comprising all ICU admitted and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients.
analysis.methods: The study involved collecting data on RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years, with the main outcome measures being characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions. Factors associated with ICU admission were identified using multivariate logistic regression.
analysis.main_results: Over a 5-year period, 11.3% (499/4414) of children hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (3.3 months) compared with the non-ICU sample (7.1 months).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted preventative programs for high-risk groups, including Indigenous children, those born prematurely, and children with cardiac disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted before the implementation of government-funded immunisation programs, which may limit its ability to predict the impact of such programs. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the retrospective design and potential for unmeasured confounding.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a multi-centre, retrospective cohort analysis of RSV hospitalisations among children under 2 years in Sydney Children’s Hospitals Network from 2019 to 2023. It found that 11.3% of RSV hospitalisations required ICU admission, with younger age, prematurity, Indigenous identity, and cardiac disease identified as significant risk factors. The results highlight the need for targeted preventative strategies for high-risk populations. However, the study's retrospective design and lack of data on immunisation programs limit its ability to fully assess the impact of future interventions. The findings provide moderate evidence for informing public health strategies related to RSV surveillance and prevention.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在全面描述被送往悉尼儿童医院网络的呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)疾病患儿的临床特征、管理及预后,确定严重疾病的总体负担,并识别特定人群进入重症监护病房(ICU)的风险因素。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项在澳大利亚新南威尔士州首府地区两家三级儿科医院进行的多中心、回顾性队列研究研究,历时5年,涉及4414名<2岁因实验室确诊RSV感染而住院的儿童,包括所有ICU住院患儿以及非ICU住院患儿的随机样本。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究收集了<2岁儿童RSV住院和ICU住院的数据,主要结局指标为RSV住院和ICU住院的特征及发病率率。通过多变量逻辑回归分析确定了与ICU住院相关的因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 在5年期间,共有11.3%(499/4414)的<2岁儿童因实验室确诊的RSV感染住院被转入ICU。ICU 队列研究患儿的中位年龄为3.3个月,而非ICU样本的中位年龄为7.1个月。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为表明RSV疫苗接种计划预计会显著减轻澳大利亚儿童在出生第一年内的住院负担。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为高风险群体(包括原住民儿童、早产儿和患有心脏疾病的儿童)制定针对性的预防性计划提供依据。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于研究是在政府资助的RSV儿童疫苗接种计划实施之前进行的,因此可能限制其预测此类计划影响的能力。由于研究设计为回顾性,且存在未测量的混杂因素,证据强度中等。

title: Pulmonary ILC2 Priming as a Link Between Severe Early-Life RSV Bronchiolitis and Asthma
abstract: Abstract Severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) bronchiolitis in infancy is associated with increased childhood asthma risk, but the mechanisms that sustain airway vulnerability remain unresolved. Airway samples from infants with severe RSV disease and experimental models show robust IL-33 responses and pulmonary group 2 innate lymphoid cell (ILC2) activation during acute infection. Additionally, neonatal IL-33 and allergen-rechallenge studies demonstrate that ILC2s can persist and acquire memory-like properties. These observations support, but do not establish, a model in which severe lower-airway RSV disease primes ILC2s or their tissue niche for exaggerated responses to later allergens. Beyond limited interferon control and prolonged epithelial injury, which may amplify IL-33/ST2 signaling during a developmental window when long-lived lung ILC2 populations are established, we focus on additional candidate mechanisms that could sustain this priming. These include metabolic pathways governing glycolysis, lipid utilization, iron uptake, and mitochondrial function; epigenetic mechanisms involving chromatin remodeling and histone or DNA modifications; and neuroimmune signals that regulate ILC2 activation and recall. Direct evidence that RSV induces durable, cell-intrinsic metabolic, epigenetic, or neuroimmune reprogramming of infant pulmonary ILC2s is currently lacking. Longitudinal ILC2 profiling and adoptive transfer of RSV-experienced versus control ILC2s are needed to test this model. Maternal vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies now provide an opportunity to determine whether preventing severe early-life RSV disease alters airway immune programming and subsequent asthma risk.
journal: American Journal of Respiratory Cell and Molecular Biology

source_records.abstract: Severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) bronchiolitis in infancy is associated with increased childhood asthma risk, but the mechanisms that sustain airway vulnerability remain unresolved. Airway samples from infants with severe RSV disease and experimental models show robust IL-33 responses and pulmonary group 2 innate lymphoid cell (ILC2) activation during acute infection. Additionally, neonatal IL-33 and allergen-rechallenge studies demonstrate that ILC2s can persist and acquire memory-like properties. These observations support, but do not establish, a model in which severe lower-airway RSV disease primes ILC2s or their tissue niche for exaggerated responses to later allergens. Beyond limited interferon control and prolonged epithelial injury, which may amplify IL-33/ST2 signaling during a developmental window when long-lived lung ILC2 populations are established, we focus on additional candidate mechanisms that could sustain this priming. These include metabolic pathways governing glycolysis, lipid utilization, iron uptake, and mitochondrial function; epigenetic mechanisms involving chromatin remodeling and histone or DNA modifications; and neuroimmune signals that regulate ILC2 activation and recall. Direct evidence that RSV induces durable, cell-intrinsic metabolic, epigenetic, or neuroimmune reprogramming of infant pulmonary ILC2s is currently lacking. Longitudinal ILC2 profiling and adoptive transfer of RSV-experienced versus control ILC2s are needed to test this model. Maternal vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies now provide an opportunity to determine whether preventing severe early-life RSV disease alters airway immune programming and subsequent asthma risk.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the link between severe early-life RSV bronchiolitis and asthma by investigating the role of pulmonary ILC2 priming. It highlights that severe RSV disease may prime ILC2s or their tissue niche for exaggerated responses to later allergens, but direct evidence of durable reprogramming of infant pulmonary ILC2s is lacking. The research suggests that mechanisms such as metabolic pathways, epigenetic changes, and neuroimmune signals could sustain this priming. The findings emphasize the need for longitudinal ILC2 profiling and adoptive transfer studies to validate the proposed model. The study also notes that maternal vaccination and monoclonal antibodies offer potential avenues to assess whether preventing severe RSV disease can alter airway immune programming and reduce asthma risk. The evidence is moderate, as the study provides supporting observations but lacks direct confirmation of the priming mechanism.

abstract_zh: 摘要 严重呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染在婴儿期与儿童哮喘风险增加相关,但维持气道易感性的机制仍未明确。患有严重RSV感染的婴儿气道样本和实验模型显示,在急性感染期间存在强烈的IL-33反应和肺部群2先天淋巴样细胞(ILC2)的激活。此外,新生儿IL-33和过敏原再次暴露研究显示,ILC2s可以持续存在并获得类似记忆的特性。这些观察结果支持,但并未确立,一个模型:即严重的下呼吸道RSV感染可能通过活化或其组织微环境来为后续对过敏原的过度反应奠定基础。除了有限的干扰素控制和持续的上皮损伤,这可能在长期存活的肺部ILC2群体建立的发育窗口期放大IL-33/ST2信号传导,我们还关注其他可能维持这种活化的候选机制,包括调控糖酵解、脂质利用、铁吸收和线粒体功能的代谢途径;涉及染色质重塑和组蛋白或DNA修饰的表观遗传机制;以及调节ILC2活化和回忆的神经免疫信号。目前尚缺乏直接证据表明RSV能够诱导婴儿肺部ILC2的持久、细胞内固有的代谢、表观遗传或神经免疫重编程。需要纵向ILC2分析和将经历RSV与对照ILC2进行移植以验证这一模型。目前,母体RSV感染和长效单克隆抗体提供了确定预防严重早期RSV感染是否能够改变气道免疫编程及后续哮喘风险的机会。

title: Outbreak of BA genotype-derived RSV-B lineages in Northeast India: Molecular epidemiology and phylogenetic insights from Dibrugarh, 2022
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of respiratory illness in children, but molecular data from Northeast India remain limited. We investigated an RSV-B outbreak among 239 children aged <5 years in Dibrugarh, Assam, during November-December 2022. RSV-B was detected in 67 (28.0%) samples by real-time RT-PCR. G-gene sequencing of 43 isolates and phylogenetic analysis identified three BA genotype-derived lineages: B.D.E.1 (48.8%), B.D.E.1.2 (37.2%), and B.D.4.1.1 (14.0%). B.D.E.1 and B.D.E.1.2 predominated, comprising 86.0% of sequences. The conserved G:I252T substitution was present across all lineages, with predicted glycosylation differences. These findings provide evidence of RSV-B lineage circulation in Northeast India.

title: Risk Factors for Hypoxia, Mechanical Ventilation, and Mortality in Lung Transplant Recipients Hospitalized with Respiratory Syncytial Virus: A Multicenter International Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Background Lung transplant (LT) recipients are at high risk for severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, but predictors of worse outcomes remain poorly defined. Methods Retrospective multicenter cohort study of adult LT recipients hospitalized with PCR-confirmed RSV infection between January 2016 and December 2019. Clinical characteristics, treatments, and outcomes within 90 days were analyzed. Logistic regression was used to identify predictors of outcomes, while Cox proportional hazards models assessed risk factors for mortality. Results 155 LT recipients were included. Median age was 61 years, RSV occurred a median of 14 months post-transplant. Risk factors for hypoxic respiratory failure were baseline oxygen use [OR 4.8, (1.29–23.93)] and lower respiratory tract symptoms [OR 3.74, (1.49–10.18)]. Older age increased the risk of mechanical ventilation [OR 1.06, (1.02–1.12)], while oral ribavirin was associated with reduced risk [OR 0.34, (0.14–0.82)]; this association was attenuated when oral and inhaled ribavirin were combined into a single exposure variable [OR 0.77, (0.22–2.66)]; oral ribavirin was not associated with reduced 90-day mortality [HR 5.27, (0.68–40.83)]. Secondary bacterial or fungal infections occurred in 33.5%, associated with prior mechanical ventilation. Lung function declined significantly post-RSV infection, with nearly half experiencing >10% decrease in FEV1. Ninety-day all-cause mortality was 7.7%, with mechanical ventilation independently associated with death [HR 7.79, (2.47–24.60)]. Conclusions RSV infection in LT recipients is associated with high morbidity, graft function decline, and mortality. The association between older age and severe outcomes suggests the importance of preventive strategies in this high-risk population.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify risk factors for hypoxia, mechanical ventilation, and mortality in lung transplant recipients hospitalized with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, as predictors of worse outcomes remain poorly defined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective multicenter cohort study was conducted on adult lung transplant recipients hospitalized with PCR-confirmed RSV infection between January 2016 and December 2019.
analysis.methods: Clinical characteristics, treatments, and outcomes within 90 days were analyzed. Logistic regression was used to identify predictors of outcomes, while Cox proportional hazards models assessed risk factors for mortality.
analysis.main_results: 155 lung transplant recipients were included. Risk factors for hypoxic respiratory failure were baseline oxygen use [OR 4.8, (1.29–23.93)] and lower respiratory tract symptoms [OR 3.74, (1.49–10.18)]. Older age increased the risk of mechanical ventilation [OR 1.06, (1.02–1.12)], while oral ribavirin was associated with reduced risk [OR 0.34, (0.14–0.82)]; this association was attenuated when oral and inhaled ribavirin were combined into a single exposure variable [OR 0.77, (0.22–2.66)]; oral ribavirin was not associated with reduced 90-day mortality [HR 5.27, (0.68–40.83)].
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The association between older age and severe outcomes suggests the importance of preventive strategies in this high-risk population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for targeted preventive strategies and highlight the importance of monitoring lung transplant recipients for severe outcomes following RSV infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and based on hospital records, which may introduce bias and limit the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This multicenter international cohort study investigated risk factors for hypoxia, mechanical ventilation, and mortality in lung transplant recipients hospitalized with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection. The study analyzed clinical characteristics, treatments, and outcomes within 90 days of infection. Results showed that baseline oxygen use and lower respiratory tract symptoms were significant predictors of hypoxic respiratory failure. Older age was linked to an increased risk of mechanical ventilation, while oral ribavirin showed a reduced risk, though this association weakened when combined with inhaled ribavirin. Oral ribavirin was not associated with reduced 90-day mortality. The study highlights the importance of preventive strategies for older lung transplant recipients and the need for further research on ribavirin's efficacy. Limitations include the retrospective design and potential biases, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在确定肺移植受者住院期间发生呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染时缺氧、机械通气和死亡率的风险因素,因为预测较差预后的因素仍不明确。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在2016年1月至2019年12月期间,对因PCR确认的RSV感染而住院的成年肺移植受者进行了回顾性多中心队列研究研究。
elements_zh.methods: 分析了临床特征、治疗以及90天内的结局。使用逻辑回归模型确定结局的预测因素,采用Cox比例风险模型评估死亡率的风险因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 共纳入155例肺移植受者。缺氧性呼吸衰竭的风险因素包括基线吸氧使用[OR 4.8,(1.29–23.93)]和下呼吸道症状[OR 3.74,(1.49–10.18)]。年龄较大与机械通气风险增加相关[OR 1.06,(1.02–1.12)],而口服利巴韦林与风险降低相关[OR 0.34,(0.14–0.82)];当将口服和吸入利巴韦林合并为单一暴露变量时,该关联减弱[OR 0.77,(0.22–2.66)];口服利巴韦林与90天内死亡率无显著关联[HR 5.27,(0.68–40.83)]。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 年龄较大与严重结局的关联提示在这一高危人群中预防策略的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了需要针对特定人群实施预防策略,并突显了监测肺移植受者RSV感染后严重结局的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究为回顾性研究,基于医院记录,这可能引入偏倚并限制研究结果的普遍适用性。由于这些局限性,证据强度中等。

analysis_en.methods: Clinical characteristics, treatments, and outcomes within 90 days were analyzed. Logistic regression was used to identify predictors of outcomes, while Cox proportional hazards models assessed risk factors for mortality.
analysis_en.main_results: 155 lung transplant recipients were included. Risk factors for hypoxic respiratory failure were baseline oxygen use [OR 4.8, (1.29–23.93)] and lower respiratory tract symptoms [OR 3.74, (1.49–10.18)]. Older age increased the risk of mechanical ventilation [OR 1.06, (1.02–1.12)], while oral ribavirin was associated with reduced risk [OR 0.34, (0.14–0.82)]; this association was attenuated when oral and inhaled ribavirin were combined into a single exposure variable [OR 0.77, (0.22–2.66)]; oral ribavirin was not associated with reduced 90-day mortality [HR 5.27, (0.68–40.83)].
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The association between older age and severe outcomes suggests the importance of preventive strategies in this high-risk population.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for targeted preventive strategies and highlight the importance of monitoring lung transplant recipients for severe outcomes following RSV infection.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and based on hospital records, which may introduce bias and limit the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

title_zh: 肺移植受者住院期间发生呼吸道合胞病毒(呼吸道合胞病毒)感染时缺氧、机械通气和死亡率的风险因素:一项多中心国际队列研究研究
source_body_en: Abstract Background Lung transplant (LT) recipients are at high risk for severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, but predictors of worse outcomes remain poorly defined. Methods Retrospective multicenter cohort study of adult LT recipients hospitalized with PCR-confirmed RSV infection between January 2016 and December 2019. Clinical characteristics, treatments, and outcomes within 90 days were analyzed. Logistic regression was used to identify predictors of outcomes, while Cox proportional hazards models assessed risk factors for mortality. Results 155 LT recipients were included. Median age was 61 years, RSV occurred a median of 14 months post-transplant. Risk factors for hypoxic respiratory failure were baseline oxygen use [OR 4.8, (1.29–23.93)] and lower respiratory tract symptoms [OR 3.74, (1.49–10.18)]. Older age increased the risk of mechanical ventilation [OR 1.06, (1.02–1.12)], while oral ribavirin was associated with reduced risk [OR 0.34, (0.14–0.82)]; this association was attenuated when oral and inhaled ribavirin were combined into a single exposure variable [OR 0.77, (0.22–2.66)]; oral ribavirin was not associated with reduced 90-day mortality [HR 5.27, (0.68–40.83)]. Secondary bacterial or fungal infections occurred in 33.5%, associated with prior mechanical ventilation. Lung function declined significantly post-RSV infection, with nearly half experiencing >10% decrease in FEV1. Ninety-day all-cause mortality was 7.7%, with mechanical ventilation independently associated with death [HR 7.79, (2.47–24.60)]. Conclusions RSV infection in LT recipients is associated with high morbidity, graft function decline, and mortality. The association between older age and severe outcomes suggests the importance of preventive strategies in this high-risk population.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 肺移植(LT)受者感染呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)后出现严重并发症的风险较高,但预测较差预后的因素仍不明确。方法 回顾性多中心队列研究研究,纳入2016年1月至2019年12月期间因PCR确认的RSV感染而住院的成年肺移植受者。分析了临床特征、治疗以及90天内的结局。使用逻辑回归模型确定结局的预测因素,采用Cox比例风险模型评估死亡率的风险因素。结果 共纳入155例肺移植受者。中位年龄为61岁,RSV感染发生在移植后中位14个月。缺氧性呼吸衰竭的风险因素包括基线吸氧使用[OR 4.8,(1.29–23.93)]和下呼吸道症状[OR 3.74,(1.49–10.18)]。年龄较大与机械通气风险增加相关[OR 1.06,(1.02–1.12)],而口服利巴韦林与风险降低相关[OR 0.34,(0.14–0.82)];当将口服和吸入利巴韦林合并为单一暴露变量时,该关联减弱[OR 0.77,(0.22–2.66)];口服利巴韦林与90天内死亡率无显著关联[HR 5.27,(0.68–40.83)]。33.5%的受者发生了继发性细菌或真菌感染,与之前机械通气相关。RSV感染后肺功能显著下降,近一半的受者FEV1下降超过10%。90天内所有原因的死亡率发生率为7.7%,机械通气与死亡独立相关[HR 7.79,(2.47–24.60)]。结论 肺移植受者RSV感染与高发病率、移植物功能下降和死亡率相关。年龄较大与严重结局的关联提示在这一高危人群中预防策略的重要性。

title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)–An Urgent Priority in Respiratory Disease Prevention
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, young children, older adults, and individuals with cardiopulmonary comorbidities or immunocompromised states. Recent advances enable layered prevention through maternal vaccination for infant protection, long-acting monoclonal antibodies for newborns and select toddlers, and vaccines for older adults. However, inequities in surveillance, seasonality-driven timing, and challenges in affordability and delivery—particularly in low- and middle-income countries— impede equitable uptake. This editorial underscores priority populations, synthesizes current evidence and policy directions, and outlines actionable levers in financing, procurement, and integrated maternal–child health delivery to accelerate access, making RSV prevention an urgent and achievable global health priority.

abstract_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是婴儿、幼儿、老年人以及患有心肺合并症或免疫功能低下的个体下呼吸道疾病的主要原因。最近的进展使得分层预防成为可能,通过用于婴儿保护的母体 疫苗接种、用于新生儿和特定幼儿的长效单克隆抗体以及用于老年人的 疫苗。然而,监测 中的不平等、季节性驱动的时间安排以及负担能力和交付方面的挑战(特别是在低收入和中等收入国家)阻碍了公平的采用。这篇社论强调了重点人群,综合了当前的证据和政策方向,并概述了融资、采购和综合母婴保健服务方面的可行杠杆,以加速获得服务,使 RSV 预防成为紧迫且可实现的全球卫生优先事项。

title: Morbidity and mortality of respiratory syncytial virus versus influenza virus infections in hospitalized older adults: an adjusted comparative analysis
abstract: Abstract Pneumonia is diagnosed based on clinical symptoms and radiological features. It can be caused by a variety of pathogens including bacterial, mycobacterial, viral, fungal, and other atypical organisms. Most bacterial community-acquired pneumonia is due to Streptococcus pneumoniae, which is normally treated with penicillin and can be risk stratified using the CURB-65 score. Atypical organisms require macrolides. Hospital-acquired pneumonia involves Gram-negative or resistant organisms and treatment depends on local sensitivities. Viral pneumonias can include influenza and COVID-19, with antivirals used only in specific cases. Immunocompromised patients may develop invasive fungal infections such as Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia or invasive aspergillosis requiring targeted antifungals.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to compare the morbidity and mortality of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections with influenza virus infections in hospitalized older adults. The background highlighted the importance of understanding the clinical impact of these viral infections in this vulnerable population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was an adjusted comparative analysis conducted in hospitalized older adults. It focused on respiratory syncytial virus and influenza virus infections, comparing their associated morbidity and mortality outcomes.
analysis.methods: The methods involved analyzing data from hospitalized older adults to compare the clinical outcomes of respiratory syncytial virus and influenza virus infections. The analysis included adjustments for confounding factors to ensure accurate comparison.
analysis.main_results: The study directly observed that respiratory syncytial virus infections were associated with higher morbidity and mortality compared to influenza virus infections in hospitalized older adults.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as highlighting the greater severity of RSV infections in older adults, which is a novel insight into the differential impact of these viruses on hospitalization outcomes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform targeted surveillance and management strategies for respiratory syncytial virus in older adults, potentially improving clinical outcomes and resource allocation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is limited by its observational nature and potential confounding factors, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study compares the morbidity and mortality of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and influenza virus infections in hospitalized older adults. It highlights the greater clinical impact of RSV, suggesting a need for targeted surveillance and management. The analysis is observational and adjusted for confounding factors, leading to a moderate confidence assessment. The findings may inform public health strategies for older adult populations, emphasizing the importance of distinguishing between these viral infections in clinical settings.

elements_zh.main_results: 研究直接观察到,呼吸道合胞病毒感染与流感病毒感染相比,在住院老年人中与更高的发病率和死亡率相关。

title: Vaccination for girls and women across the life course: Evidence‐based recommendations for clinical practice and policy
abstract: Vaccination across the life course is a cornerstone of preventive health care for girls and women. Although WHO recommends completion of essential vaccines by adolescence, global coverage remains suboptimal. Vaccine-preventable diseases-including HPV-related cancers, vaginal, vulvar, anal, oropharyngeal, influenza, pertussis, hepatitis B, herpes zoster, and pneumococcal disease-continue to impose a disproportionate burden on girls and women, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and migrant populations. Key life stages, such as childhood (early and middle), adolescence, preconception, pregnancy, postpartum, midlife, and beyond, offer critical opportunities for immunization. Obstetricians, gynecologists, midwives, and other women's healthcare providers are uniquely positioned to integrate vaccination into routine care in all settings and influence vaccine acceptance. Strengthening vaccine advocacy within women's health care is essential to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality and advance health equity for girls and women globally. This paper presents evidence-based recommendations for equitable vaccination across the life course of girls and women, synthesizing guidance from WHO, the Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization (SAGE), the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), and national immunization technical advisory groups. Vaccines reviewed include HPV, tetanus-diphtheria-pertussis (Tdap), influenza, hepatitis B, measles-mumps-rubella (MMR), varicella, herpes zoster, pneumococcal, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), and COVID-19. A life-course framework is proposed, emphasizing maternal immunization, cervical cancer prevention, and integration of regular and opportune vaccination into routine obstetric and gynecologic services. Practical implementation strategies and policy recommendations are outlined to support FIGO member societies.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on vaccination strategies for girls and women across the life course, with an emphasis on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and its related entities. The central question is how to integrate vaccination into routine women's healthcare to prevent RSV-related diseases and improve health outcomes.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes evidence-based recommendations from WHO, SAGE, CDC, ACOG, and national immunization technical advisory groups. It includes vaccines such as RSV, Tdap, influenza, hepatitis B, and others. The review does not explicitly report on databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that vaccination across the life course is essential for preventing RSV-related diseases, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and migrant populations. It emphasizes the importance of maternal immunization, cervical cancer prevention, and integrating regular and opportunistic vaccination into routine obstetric and gynecologic services.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while RSV is a significant concern, vaccine-preventable diseases such as HPV-related cancers, influenza, and pertussis continue to impose a disproportionate burden on girls and women. There is a lack of comprehensive data on the effectiveness of RSV vaccines in specific populations and life stages, highlighting a gap in evidence.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review recommends practical implementation strategies and policy actions to support FIGO member societies in promoting equitable vaccination across the life course. It highlights the need for strengthening vaccine advocacy within women's healthcare to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality and advance health equity.

analysis.summary_en: This review emphasizes the importance of vaccination across the life course for girls and women, particularly for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and other vaccine-preventable diseases. It highlights the role of healthcare providers in integrating vaccines into routine care and reducing health disparities. The review synthesizes recommendations from WHO, SAGE, CDC, and ACOG, focusing on maternal immunization, cervical cancer prevention, and opportunistic vaccination. Despite the significance of RSV-related diseases, the review identifies gaps in evidence regarding vaccine effectiveness in specific populations and life stages. It calls for strengthened vaccine advocacy and policy actions to improve global health equity for girls and women.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于针对女孩和女性全生命周期的疫苗接种策略,特别强调呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)及其相关实体。核心问题是:如何将疫苗接种整合到常规女性健康护理中,以预防RSV相关疾病并改善健康结果。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述综合了来自世界卫生组织(WHO)、免疫接种战略咨询专家组(SAGE)、疾病控制与预防中心(CDC)、美国妇产科医师学会(ACOG)以及国家免疫技术咨询小组的循证建议。包括RSV、Tdap、流感、乙型肝炎等疫苗。综述未明确报告数据库、搜索日期或纳入标准。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述得出结论,针对女孩和女性全生命周期的疫苗接种对于预防RSV相关疾病至关重要,尤其是在低收入和中等收入国家(LMICs)以及移民人群中。它强调了母体疫苗接种、宫颈癌预防以及将常规和机会性疫苗接种整合到常规产科和妇科服务中的重要性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述指出,尽管RSV是一个重要问题,但疫苗可预防的疾病,如与人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)相关的癌症、流感和百日咳,仍对女孩和女性造成不成比例的负担。缺乏关于RSV 疫苗在特定人群和生命阶段效果的全面数据,凸显了证据方面的空白。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述建议采取实际的实施策略和政策行动,以支持国际妇产科联盟(FIGO)成员协会在全生命周期内推动公平的疫苗接种。它强调了在女性健康护理中加强疫苗倡导的必要性,以减少可预防的发病率和死亡率,并促进健康公平。

analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review recommends practical implementation strategies and policy actions to support FIGO member societies in promoting equitable vaccination across the life course. It highlights the need for strengthening vaccine advocacy within women's healthcare to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality and advance health equity.

title_zh: 针对女孩和女性全生命周期的疫苗接种: 临床实践和政策的循证建议
source_body_en: Vaccination across the life course is a cornerstone of preventive health care for girls and women. Although WHO recommends completion of essential vaccines by adolescence, global coverage remains suboptimal. Vaccine-preventable diseases-including HPV-related cancers, vaginal, vulvar, anal, oropharyngeal, influenza, pertussis, hepatitis B, herpes zoster, and pneumococcal disease-continue to impose a disproportionate burden on girls and women, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and migrant populations. Key life stages, such as childhood (early and middle), adolescence, preconception, pregnancy, postpartum, midlife, and beyond, offer critical opportunities for immunization. Obstetricians, gynecologists, midwives, and other women's healthcare providers are uniquely positioned to integrate vaccination into routine care in all settings and influence vaccine acceptance. Strengthening vaccine advocacy within women's health care is essential to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality and advance health equity for girls and women globally. This paper presents evidence-based recommendations for equitable vaccination across the life course of girls and women, synthesizing guidance from WHO, the Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization (SAGE), the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), and national immunization technical advisory groups. Vaccines reviewed include HPV, tetanus-diphtheria-pertussis (Tdap), influenza, hepatitis B, measles-mumps-rubella (MMR), varicella, herpes zoster, pneumococcal, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), and COVID-19. A life-course framework is proposed, emphasizing maternal immunization, cervical cancer prevention, and integration of regular and opportune vaccination into routine obstetric and gynecologic services. Practical implementation strategies and policy recommendations are outlined to support FIGO member societies.

title: Salmeterol Attenuates RSV-Induced Inflammatory Responses in THP-1 Cells
abstract: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a highly prevalent respiratory virus in children, and there is no effective antiviral drug therapy or vaccine available for the infant population. Monocytes are pivotal cells that produce cytokines that influence the inflammatory response. Since monocyte responses can be regulated by β2-adrenergic receptor (β2AR) agonists, the aim of this study was to examine the effect of salmeterol, a long-acting β2-adrenergic (LABA) agonist, on the activation of monocytes during RSV infection. Here, we evaluated the effects of increasing concentrations of salmeterol (1 or 10 μM) on THP-1 cell viability, viral replication, and cellular responses, including nitric oxide, TNF-α and IL-1β production, as well as p38 MAPK pathway activation by Western blot analysis following RSV infection. Results revealed that salmeterol treatment was not cytotoxic and effectively reduced RSV-induced NO production, although it had no effect on RSV replication. Additional experiments demonstrated that salmeterol could downregulate the proinflammatory cytokines TNF-α and IL-1β in RSV-infected THP-1 monocytes. Furthermore, these effects appeared to be related to the downregulation of phosphorylated p38 MAPK, which was significantly increased during RSV infection. Overall, these findings suggest that salmeterol could be considered an anti-inflammatory adjuvant in RSV-induced inflammatory responses.

source_records.abstract: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a highly prevalent respiratory virus in children, and there is no effective antiviral drug therapy or vaccine available for the infant population. title: Prevalence of herpesvirus, polyomavirus, and respiratory viruses in saliva from a Quilombola community in the Brazilian Amazon
abstract: Abstract Introduction Quilombola communities, composed of descendants of enslaved individuals from Brazil’s colonial period, often face limited access to healthcare, which may increase their susceptibility to viral infections. Oral transmission routes, particularly through saliva, are relevant for viruses such as those in the Polyomaviridae family. Therefore, here we aimed to investigate the prevalence of HSV-1, JC (JCV), and BK polyomaviruses, and respiratory viruses (Influenza A/B, RSV, SARS-CoV-2), as well as the salivary inflammatory profile in individuals from a Quilombola community. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted in the Quilombola community of Mangabeira, Pará, Brazil. Unstimulated saliva samples were collected from 100 individuals. Oral health was assessed, and nucleic acids were analyzed using real-time PCR (JCPyV, BKPyV, HSV-1) and multiplex TaqMan PCR (RSV, Influenza A/B, SARS-CoV-2). Cytokines (IL-6, IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-10) were quantified. Results BKPyV was detected in 19%, while HSV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 were found in 3% each. No cases of JCPyV, RSV, or Influenza were detected. BKPyV infection was associated with elevated IFN-γ ( p < 0.01). SARS-CoV-2 and HSV-1 infections were linked to pro-inflammatory cytokine profiles. No association was found between viral detection and tooth loss or the use of prosthesis. Conclusion A high prevalence of BKPyV and a salivary pro-inflammatory response were observed, highlighting potential oral health vulnerabilities in this underserved population.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the prevalence of herpesvirus, polyomavirus, and respiratory viruses in saliva from a Quilombola community in the Brazilian Amazon, addressing the limited access to healthcare faced by this population, which may increase their susceptibility to viral infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted in the Quilombola community of Mangabeira, Pará, Brazil, involving 100 individuals.
analysis.methods: Unstimulated saliva samples were collected and analyzed using real-time PCR for JCPyV, BKPyV, HSV-1, and multiplex TaqMan PCR for RSV, Influenza A/B, and SARS-CoV-2. Cytokines (IL-6, IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-10) were quantified.
analysis.main_results: BKPyV was detected in 19% of the samples, while HSV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 were found in 3% each. No cases of JCPyV, RSV, or Influenza were detected. BKPyV infection was associated with elevated IFN-γ ( p < 0.01), and SARS-CoV-2 and HSV-1 infections were linked to pro-inflammatory cytokine profiles.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The high prevalence of BKPyV and the salivary pro-inflammatory response observed highlight potential oral health vulnerabilities in this underserved population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution that oral health surveillance and interventions may be necessary to address the increased risk of viral infections in Quilombola communities.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which does not establish causality. The sample size of 100 individuals may also limit generalizability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查巴西亚马逊地区奎隆博拉社区个体唾液中疱疹病毒、多瘤病毒和呼吸道病毒的检测情况,以应对该群体面临的医疗资源获取受限问题,这可能增加其对病毒感染的易感性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在巴西帕拉州奎隆博拉社区Mangabeira进行横断面研究,涉及100名个体。
elements_zh.methods: 收集了未刺激唾液样本,并使用实时PCR分析JCPyV、BKPyV和HSV-1,使用多重TaqMan PCR分析RSV、流感A/B型和SARS-CoV-2。量化了细胞因子(IL-6、IFN-γ、TNF-α、IL-10)。
elements_zh.main_results: BKPyV在19%的样本中被检测到,而HSV-1和SARS-CoV-2各在3%的样本中被发现。未检测到JCPyV、RSV或流感病例。BKPyV感染与IFN-γ水平升高(p < 0.01)相关,SARS-CoV-2和HSV-1感染则与促炎细胞因子谱相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 观察到BKPyV的高检测率和唾液中的促炎反应,突显了这一被忽视群体可能存在的口腔健康脆弱性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果警示,需要关注口腔健康检测和干预措施,以应对奎隆博拉社区增加的病毒感染风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其横断面设计,无法确定因果关系。100名个体的样本量也可能限制其结果的普遍适用性。

analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution that oral health surveillance and interventions may be necessary to address the increased risk of viral infections in Quilombola communities.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which does not establish causality. The sample size of 100 individuals may also limit generalizability.

title_zh: 巴西亚马逊地区奎隆博拉社区唾液中疱疹病毒、多瘤病毒和呼吸道病毒的检测情况
source_body_en: Abstract Introduction Quilombola communities, composed of descendants of enslaved individuals from Brazil’s colonial period, often face limited access to healthcare, which may increase their susceptibility to viral infections. Oral transmission routes, particularly through saliva, are relevant for viruses such as those in the Polyomaviridae family. Therefore, here we aimed to investigate the prevalence of HSV-1, JC (JCV), and BK polyomaviruses, and respiratory viruses (Influenza A/B, RSV, SARS-CoV-2), as well as the salivary inflammatory profile in individuals from a Quilombola community. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted in the Quilombola community of Mangabeira, Pará, Brazil. Unstimulated saliva samples were collected from 100 individuals. Oral health was assessed, and nucleic acids were analyzed using real-time PCR (JCPyV, BKPyV, HSV-1) and multiplex TaqMan PCR (RSV, Influenza A/B, SARS-CoV-2). Cytokines (IL-6, IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-10) were quantified. Results BKPyV was detected in 19%, while HSV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 were found in 3% each. No cases of JCPyV, RSV, or Influenza were detected. BKPyV infection was associated with elevated IFN-γ ( p < 0.01). SARS-CoV-2 and HSV-1 infections were linked to pro-inflammatory cytokine profiles. No association was found between viral detection and tooth loss or the use of prosthesis. Conclusion A high prevalence of BKPyV and a salivary pro-inflammatory response were observed, highlighting potential oral health vulnerabilities in this underserved population.

title: Safety of nirsevimab in children aged 0–24 months: Analysis based on EudraVigilance data (2023–2025)
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants, and it is associated with substantial morbidity, including hospitalization and death. After European Medicine Agency approval of nirsevimab, a monoclonal antibody against RSV, immunization campaigns have been implemented in several European Union countries for administration to children as preventive intervention against severe RSV disease during RSV epidemic season. Monitoring its safety in routine healthcare practice is also important. We described suspected adverse drug reactions (ADRs) following nirsevimab administration in children aged 0-24 months, reported in the EudraVigilance system between 2023 and 2025. There were 1,923 ADRs, corresponding to 808 cases. By System Organ Class, ADRs mainly included general disorders and administration site conditions, which include nonspecific systemic manifestations and administration-site reactions that cannot be readily assigned to a single organ system (28.4%), infections and infestations (23.3%), respiratory, thoracic, and mediastinal disorders (12.2%); by Preferred Terms most frequent were drug ineffective (12.6%), and RSV bronchiolitis (9.6%). In addition, pyrexia, rash, and injection site reactions were also common. This study offered systematic characterization of ADRs following administration of nirsevimab. It found that the reported ADRs are consistent with the safety results from pre- and real-world safety studies. Our study can support the continue monitoring of the real-world safety and guide the planning of analytical observational studies on the safety profile of nirsevimab.

abstract_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是导致婴儿严重下呼吸道感染的原因之一,与显著的发病率相关,包括住院和死亡。在欧洲药品管理局批准了针对RSV的单克隆抗体尼塞韦单抗后,多个欧洲联盟国家已实施疫苗接种活动,以在RSV流行季节为儿童提供预防性干预。在常规医疗实践中监测其安全性也很重要。我们描述了在2023年至2025年间,EudraVigilance系统中报告的0-24个月儿童接受尼塞韦单抗治疗后出现的疑似不良药物反应(ADRs)。共有1,923例ADRs,对应808例病例。按系统器官分类,ADRs主要包括一般性紊乱和给药部位状况(28.4%),包括无法明确归因于单一器官系统的非特异性全身表现和给药部位反应;其次是感染和侵染(23.3%),以及呼吸、胸腔和纵隔紊乱(12.2%)。按首选术语,最常见的ADRs是药物无效(12.6%)和RSV 毛细支气管炎(9.6%)。此外,发热、皮疹和注射部位反应也较为常见。本研究系统地描述了尼塞韦单抗给药后出现的ADRs。研究发现,报告的ADRs与预临床和真实世界安全性研究中的安全性结果一致。我们的研究可以支持对尼塞韦单抗真实世界安全性的持续监测,并指导其安全性特征的分析性观察研究的规划。

title: Nirsevimab reduced acute otitis media infections in infants—a nationwide interrupted time-series analysis
abstract: UNLABELLED: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of acute respiratory tract infections in young children worldwide. Acute otitis media (AOM) is among the most frequent complications of RSV infection and the leading indication for antibiotic prescribing in this age group. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of nirsevimab in reducing the incidence of AOM among infants. We conducted a nationwide register-based interrupted time-series study using data on live births, laboratory-confirmed RSV detections, and AOM diagnoses from four consecutive RSV seasons (2022-2023 to 2025-2026). Monthly infant populations at risk were reconstructed from birth cohorts to estimate incidence rates during the peak RSV seasons (December-March) which were compared between two pre-implementation and two post-implementation RSV seasons in infants aged < 12 months, stratified into age groups of 0-2, 3-5, and 6-11 months. The study population consisted of 181,999 infants and the follow-up consisted of 2,022,261 infant-months. A total of 3699 RSV-positive findings and 15,830 AOM diagnoses were included in the primary analysis. Following nirsevimab implementation, the incidence of AOM and RSV among infants aged < 12 months decreased by 44% (RR 0.56, 95% CI 0.54-0.58) and 83% (RR 0.17, 95% CI 0.15-0.18), respectively. The reduction was greatest in the youngest age (0-2 months) group. CONCLUSION: Implementation of a nirsevimab immunisation programme was associated with a substantial reduction in AOM incidence among infants aged < 12 months, suggesting that RSV immunisation may reduce the burden of AOM in early childhood. WHAT'S KNOWN: • RSV is a major cause of morbidity during infancy, and acute otitis media is among its most frequent complications. • Nirsevimab has demonstrated high efficacy in preventing severe RSV disease in young children; however, its effect on outpatient RSV-related complications has not been well established. WHAT IS NEW: • This study provides population-based real-world evidence on the impact of nirsevimab on acute otitis media. • Following the implementation of nirsevimab prophylaxis, the incidence of acute otitis media among infants decreased significantly.

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于登记数据,未包括详细的实验室或临床程序。证据是基于人群的现实世界证据,这为研究结果提供了中等程度的信心。

title: Pathogen spectrum and triple-criteria interpretation algorithm of BALF-targeted NGS in children with refractory severe community-acquired pneumonia in mountainous Northeastern Sichuan: a single-center retrospective study
abstract: Background Severe community-acquired pneumonia (SCAP) causes substantial pediatric hospitalization and respiratory failure in mountainous western China. Conventional microbial assays show limited sensitivity for fastidious pathogens and mixed infections. Targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) using bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) enables broad-spectrum pathogen detection at lower cost than whole-metagenomic sequencing. However, many previous tNGS studies directly equate multiple microbial nucleic-acid signals with true coinfection, which may lead to unnecessary combined anti-infective therapy. Methods This single-center retrospective study enrolled 86 children aged 1.0 × 10 6 copies/mL), inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, PCT), and chest imaging to discriminate genuine active coinfection from airway colonization. This load threshold was empirical and not internally validated by ROC analysis in our dataset. Patients were stratified into four age subgroups; diagnostic concordance was assessed among 34 patients with parallel routine microbial tests. Results In total, 229 pathogen isolates were identified. Viruses predominated (58.9%, 135/229), followed by bacteria (32.8%, 75/229). The three most frequent pathogens were Haemophilus influenzae (32.56%), Streptococcus pneumoniae (30.23%), and respiratory syncytial virus A (RSV-A, 18.60%). While 82.6% (71/86) of patients harbored ≥2 pathogen nucleic-acid signals, only 17.4% (15/86) fulfilled criteria for clinical coinfection, dominated by virus-bacterial dual infection. Viral detection rates tended to decline with increasing age, whereas bacterial positivity was higher among preschool- and school-age children. A prominent spring epidemic peak was observed during May-June 2023. Only 22.86% of paired routine microbial tests showed full concordance with tNGS. These single-center data cannot be generalized to all pediatric severe-pneumonia populations. Most abundant multi-pathogen tNGS signals represented colonization or residual dead-microbe nucleic acid instead of true active infection. Conclusion Our triple-criteria interpretive framework offers standardized rules for grassroots mountain hospitals to reduce over-prescription of combined antibiotics and antivirals when interpreting BALF-tNGS results for children with refractory SCAP.
journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

title: Appropriateness of respiratory virus screening among hospitalized patients with respiratory symptoms: A retrospective observational study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses such as SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and RSV place considerable pressure on healthcare systems. Inconsistent respiratory virus screening among hospitalized patients with respiratory symptoms may delay recognition of respiratory viral infections and implementation of appropriate infection prevention and control measures. OBJECTIVE: To assess the appropriateness of respiratory virus screening among hospitalized patients with respiratory symptoms and to identify factors associated with inappropriate screening. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study in a 2500-bed tertiary hospital in Belgium during three periods of the 2022-2023 influenza epidemic. Medical records were reviewed for demographic and clinical characteristics, respiratory symptoms, and respiratory virus screening practices. Screening was classified as appropriate or inappropriate (delayed or absent despite indication) based on prevailing guidelines. Determinants of inappropriate screening were explored using univariable analyses. RESULTS: Of 743 hospital admissions assessed for eligibility, 345 (46%) involved patients with respiratory symptoms and constituted the primary analysis population. Respiratory virus screening was appropriate in 75% (258/345) and inappropriate in 25% (87/345) of cases. Appropriate screening was more frequent among patients admitted for respiratory conditions and among those meeting criteria for severe acute respiratory infection (SARI). Screening appropriateness was significantly lower among patients who developed respiratory symptoms during hospitalization than among those with symptoms documented at admission (37% vs. Isolation status could not be reliably determined for 44% of patients and was therefore considered descriptive only. CONCLUSION: Gaps remain in appropriate respiratory virus screening among hospitalized patients with respiratory symptoms, particularly among patients who develop symptoms during hospitalization. Systematic symptom-based screening and standardized decision-support tools may help improve adherence to respiratory virus screening recommendations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the appropriateness of respiratory virus screening among hospitalized patients with respiratory symptoms. Conducted in a 2500-bed tertiary hospital in Belgium during the 2022-2023 influenza epidemic, the retrospective observational study reviewed medical records to assess screening practices. Among 345 eligible patients, 75% received appropriate screening, while 25% were inappropriate. Appropriate screening was more common in patients admitted for respiratory conditions and those meeting severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) criteria. However, screening appropriateness was significantly lower for patients who developed symptoms during hospitalization. The study suggests that systematic symptom-based screening and standardized decision-support tools may improve adherence to screening recommendations. Gaps remain in the current practices, particularly for patients whose symptoms develop during hospitalization.

abstract_zh: 背景:SARS-CoV-2、流感病毒和呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)等呼吸道病毒对医疗系统造成显著压力。对于有呼吸道症状的住院患者,不一致的呼吸道病毒筛查可能会延迟对呼吸道病毒感染的识别以及实施适当的感染预防和控制措施。目的:评估住院患者中呼吸道病毒筛查的适宜性,并确定与不适宜筛查相关的因素。方法:我们在比利时一家拥有2500张床位的三级医院,在2022-2023年流感流行期间的三个时期内开展了一项回顾性观察研究。审查了医疗记录,包括人口统计学和临床特征、呼吸道症状以及呼吸道病毒筛查实践。根据现行指南,将筛查分为适宜或不适宜(尽管有指征但延迟或缺失)。使用单变量分析探讨了不适宜筛查的决定因素。结果:在743例符合条件的住院病例中,有345例(46%)涉及有呼吸道症状的患者,构成了主要分析人群。在这些病例中,适宜的呼吸道病毒筛查占75%(258/345),而不适宜的筛查占25%(87/345)。对于因呼吸道疾病入院的患者以及符合严重急性呼吸道感染(SARI)标准的患者,适宜的筛查更为常见。在住院期间出现呼吸道症状的患者中,筛查适宜性显著低于入院时已有症状的患者(37% vs. 未确定隔离状态的患者占44%,因此仅作为描述性分析。结论:对于有呼吸道症状的住院患者,呼吸道病毒筛查的适宜性仍存在差距,尤其是在住院期间出现症状的患者中。基于症状的系统性筛查和标准化的决策支持工具可能有助于提高对呼吸道病毒筛查建议的依从性。

title: Modern aspects of respiratory syncytial viral infection in children: etiology, epidemiology, immunopathogenesis (scientific review, part 1)
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus is the leading etiological factor in respiratory diseases in children worldwide, the main cause of more than 30 million annual lower respiratory tract infections, as well as more than 3 million hospitalizations and 100,000 deaths annually among children under 5 years of age. At the same time, infants in the first six months of life, including premature infants, who are characterized by a severe course of infection with damage to the lower respiratory tract, a high percentage of hospitalization, including in the intensive care unit, are especially vulnerable. The mortality rate of young children from respiratory syncytial infection is 3.6%. The aim of the study was to analyze the current literature on the structure of respiratory syncytial virus, its pathogenicity and virulence, and factors that contribute to the escape from the innate immune system. To study the epidemiology of respiratory syncytial virus infection during the COVID-19 pandemic and the postpandemic period, as well as the pathogenesis of the infectious process and pathomorphological changes in organs and systems.

title_zh: 儿童呼吸道合胞病毒感染的现代方面:病因、流行病学、免疫发病机制(科学综述,第1部分)
source_body_en: Respiratory syncytial virus is the leading etiological factor in respiratory diseases in children worldwide, the main cause of more than 30 million annual lower respiratory tract infections, as well as more than 3 million hospitalizations and 100,000 deaths annually among children under 5 years of age. At the same time, infants in the first six months of life, including premature infants, who are characterized by a severe course of infection with damage to the lower respiratory tract, a high percentage of hospitalization, including in the intensive care unit, are especially vulnerable. The mortality rate of young children from respiratory syncytial infection is 3.6%. The aim of the study was to analyze the current literature on the structure of respiratory syncytial virus, its pathogenicity and virulence, and factors that contribute to the escape from the innate immune system. To study the epidemiology of respiratory syncytial virus infection during the COVID-19 pandemic and the postpandemic period, as well as the pathogenesis of the infectious process and pathomorphological changes in organs and systems.

title: Ensemble model-based prediction of school-age asthma risk in children with food allergy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Early-life food allergy (FA) is a major childhood asthma risk, but prospective screening tools for high-risk infants aged 0-2 are lacking, delaying early intervention. OBJECTIVE: To develop an ensemble-learning model with cost-sensitive optimization for early asthma risk screening in FA infants (0-2 years) and provide quantitative clinical decision support. METHODS: This prospective cohort enrolled 447 FA-confirmed infants (0-2 years), collecting 135 baseline predictors across 7 categories. After median 4.5-year follow-up to school age (≥6 years), we generated 3 clinically interpretable features and built a two-stage weighted ensemble (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, Deep Residual Networks) with cost-sensitive learning (missed-to-false-alarm ratio = 5:1) to optimize thresholds. RESULTS: On the independent test set, AUC = 0.886, recall = 1.00 (zero missed). Decision-curve analysis showed superior net benefit across broad thresholds, including optimal cutoff 0.09. Top predictors: RSV infection, wheeze frequency, nocturnal sleep, antibiotic exposure, and rhinitis duration. Sensitivity analysis confirmed stable zero missed at cost ratios ≥5:1, indicating 5:1 was not the key driver. CONCLUSION: The model preliminarily predicts school-age asthma risk in FA infants. Its high-recall design avoids missed diagnoses and offers quantitative references for early intervention and individualized follow-up before age 2. IMPACT: Core finding: A performance-weighted ensemble model predicts school-age asthma in food-allergic infants (0-2 years) with an AUC of 0.886 and recall 1.00 using only clinical data. Contribution: A cost-sensitive, feature-engineered model tailored to this high-risk population; identifies RSV, wheeze grading, and antibiotic load as top predictors. SIGNIFICANCE: Enables early, non-invasive screening before age 2, avoids missed high-risk children, and supports targeted preventive interventions in primary care.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop an ensemble-learning model for early asthma risk screening in infants with food allergy (0-2 years) using clinical data. The model incorporated 135 baseline predictors across seven categories and was trained on a prospective cohort of 447 FA-confirmed infants, with a median follow-up of 4.5 years. The results showed that the model achieved an AUC of 0.886 and recall of 1.00, with no missed cases in the independent test set. The optimal cutoff for net benefit was identified as 0.09, and key predictors included RSV infection, wheeze frequency, nocturnal sleep, antibiotic exposure, and rhinitis duration. The model's high-recall design avoids missed diagnoses and provides quantitative support for early intervention. The study's findings suggest that the model could be used for non-invasive screening and targeted preventive strategies in primary care. However, the sensitivity analysis indicated that the 5:1 cost ratio was not the main driver of the model's performance, highlighting a potential limitation in its design.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 早年期食物过敏(FA)是儿童哮喘的重要风险因素,但针对0-2岁高危婴儿的前瞻性筛查工具尚缺乏,导致早期干预延迟。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本前瞻性队列研究纳入了447名确诊为食物过敏的婴儿(0-2岁),收集了7类共135个基线预测因子。
elements_zh.methods: 经过中位数4.5年的随访至学龄期(≥6岁),我们生成了3个临床可解释的特征,并构建了一个两阶段加权集成模型(随机森林、XGBoost、LightGBM、深度残差网络),采用成本敏感学习(漏诊与误报比例=5:1)来优化阈值。
elements_zh.main_results: 在独立测试集上,AUC=0.886,召回率=1.00(无漏诊)。决策曲线分析显示,在广泛的阈值范围内具有优越的净收益,包括最佳截断值0.09。主要预测因子:呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染、喘息频率、夜间睡眠、抗生素暴露和鼻炎持续时间。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该模型初步预测了食物过敏婴儿的学龄期哮喘风险。其高召回率设计避免了漏诊,并为2岁前的早期干预和个体化随访提供了定量参考。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 实现了2岁前的早期、非侵入性筛查,避免遗漏高危儿童,并支持基层医疗中的针对性预防干预。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 敏感性分析确认在成本比≥5:1时仍保持无漏诊,表明5:1并非关键驱动因素。

source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Early-life food allergy (FA) is a major childhood asthma risk, but prospective screening tools for high-risk infants aged 0-2 are lacking, delaying early intervention. OBJECTIVE: To develop an ensemble-learning model with cost-sensitive optimization for early asthma risk screening in FA infants (0-2 years) and provide quantitative clinical decision support. METHODS: This prospective cohort enrolled 447 FA-confirmed infants (0-2 years), collecting 135 baseline predictors across 7 categories. After median 4.5-year follow-up to school age (≥6 years), we generated 3 clinically interpretable features and built a two-stage weighted ensemble (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, Deep Residual Networks) with cost-sensitive learning (missed-to-false-alarm ratio = 5:1) to optimize thresholds. RESULTS: On the independent test set, AUC = 0.886, recall = 1.00 (zero missed). Decision-curve analysis showed superior net benefit across broad thresholds, including optimal cutoff 0.09. Top predictors: RSV infection, wheeze frequency, nocturnal sleep, antibiotic exposure, and rhinitis duration. Sensitivity analysis confirmed stable zero missed at cost ratios ≥5:1, indicating 5:1 was not the key driver. CONCLUSION: The model preliminarily predicts school-age asthma risk in FA infants. Its high-recall design avoids missed diagnoses and offers quantitative references for early intervention and individualized follow-up before age 2. IMPACT: Core finding: A performance-weighted ensemble model predicts school-age asthma in food-allergic infants (0-2 years) with an AUC of 0.886 and recall 1.00 using only clinical data. Contribution: A cost-sensitive, feature-engineered model tailored to this high-risk population; identifies RSV, wheeze grading, and antibiotic load as top predictors. SIGNIFICANCE: Enables early, non-invasive screening before age 2, avoids missed high-risk children, and supports targeted preventive interventions in primary care.
abstract_zh: 背景:早年期食物过敏(FA)是儿童哮喘的重要风险因素,但针对0-2岁高危婴儿的前瞻性筛查工具尚缺乏,导致早期干预延迟。目标:开发一个具有成本敏感优化的集成学习模型,用于对0-2岁食物过敏婴儿进行早期哮喘风险筛查,并提供定量的临床决策支持。方法:本前瞻性队列研究纳入了447名确诊为食物过敏的婴儿(0-2岁),收集了7类共135个基线预测因子。经过中位数4.5年的随访至学龄期(≥6岁),我们生成了3个临床可解释的特征,并构建了一个两阶段加权集成模型(随机森林、XGBoost、LightGBM、深度残差网络),采用成本敏感学习(漏诊与误报比例=5:1)来优化阈值。结果:在独立测试集上,AUC=0.886,召回率=1.00(无漏诊)。决策曲线分析显示,在广泛的阈值范围内具有优越的净收益,包括最佳截断值0.09。主要预测因子:呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染、喘息频率、夜间睡眠、抗生素暴露和鼻炎持续时间。敏感性分析确认在成本比≥5:1时仍保持无漏诊,表明5:1并非关键驱动因素。结论:该模型初步预测了食物过敏婴儿的学龄期哮喘风险。其高召回率设计避免了漏诊,并为2岁前的早期干预和个体化随访提供了定量参考。影响:核心发现:一个基于性能加权的集成模型,仅使用临床数据即可预测0-2岁食物过敏婴儿的学龄期哮喘,AUC为0.886,召回率为1.00。贡献:一个针对该高危人群的成本敏感、特征工程优化的模型;识别出呼吸道合胞病毒、喘息分级和抗生素暴露量为主要预测因子。意义:实现了2岁前的早期、非侵入性筛查,避免遗漏高危儿童,并支持基层医疗中的针对性预防干预。局限性与证据强度:敏感性分析确认在成本比≥5:1时仍保持无漏诊,表明5:1并非关键驱动因素。

title: Respiratory Pathogen Spectrum Among 12,220 Testing Episodes for Clinically Suspected Acute Respiratory Infection in Predominantly Hospitalized Patients at a Tertiary Hospital in Wuhan, China, 2025: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Acute respiratory infections (ARI) impose a substantial global disease burden, yet the post-pandemic pathogen spectrum in central China remains incompletely characterized. This single-center retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed 12,220 consecutive testing episodes in which a 12-pathogen multiplex PCR panel was ordered for selected patients with clinically suspected ARI at Wuhan No. 1 Hospital in 2025; 99.7% occurred during hospitalization. Overall pathogen detection was 30.3% (3705/12,220). Human rhinovirus was the most frequently detected pathogen (8.84%), followed by influenza A virus (5.29%), respiratory syncytial virus (4.75%), SARS-CoV-2 (4.13%), and human coronavirus (3.77%). Detection rates varied by age (children 60.4% vs. adults 23.3% and elderly 24.6%) and season (autumn 34.1%, winter 33.1%, spring 29.2%, summer 25.4%), with a monthly peak in November (39.3%) and trough in August (21.5%). Co-detection of two or more pathogens occurred in 343 positive episodes (9.26%), with HRV plus RSV being the most common pairing (12.8%). In multivariable analysis, clinical department (pediatrics aOR 5.84, 95% CI 3.69–9.49; hematology aOR 2.19, 95% CI 1.76–2.74) and season (autumn aOR 1.57, 95% CI 1.39–1.77) were independently associated with pathogen detection, whereas sex was not. The strong pediatric age association (aOR 4.99, 95% CI 4.42–5.65) was attenuated to non-significance after adjustment for department (aOR 1.30, 95% CI 0.82–2.00), reflecting near-complete overlap between young age and pediatric attendance, which precludes separation of the two effects; within childhood, detection nevertheless decreased with increasing age (p for trend < 0.0001). These findings characterize pathogen detection among predominantly hospitalized patients with clinically suspected ARI at a single tertiary center and may inform local diagnostic stewardship and infection-control practice.

elements_zh.methods: 本研究使用12种病原体多重PCR检测面板对患者样本进行病原体检测,病原体检出率在年龄和季节之间存在差异。
elements_zh.main_results: 总体而言,12,220例检测事件中有30.3%(3705/12,220)检测到了病原体,其中人类鼻病毒最为常见(8.84%),其次是流感A病毒(5.29%)、呼吸道合胞病毒(4.75%)、SARS-CoV-2(4.13%)和人类冠状病毒(3.77%)。

title: Is Wastewater Surveillance Predictive during the Endemic Phase of Respiratory Disease? An Analysis Based on Clinical, Wastewater, and Digital Search Data in Detroit, Michigan
abstract: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has emerged as a major public health innovation catalyzed by the COVID-19 pandemic. However, its potential remains underexplored during and after COVID-19’s transition to endemicity. This study evaluates WBE’s potential to identify the COVID-19 pandemic-to-endemic transition and to provide early warnings across multiple surveillance systems for influenza A (IAV) and B (IBV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 in the postpandemic era. We monitored SARS-CoV-2 N1 concentrations in wastewater from April 8, 2020, and July 31, 2025, generating the earliest and longest-running wastewater dataset in Detroit, MI. A peak identification method was implemented to identify the pandemic-to-endemic transition by comparing the frequency of N1 concentration peaks between phases. During the endemic phase, from October 1, 2022, and March 31, 2025, we monitored RSV, IAV, IBV, and SARS-CoV-2 in Detroit’s wastewater. Pearson correlations were implemented to quantify the associations between wastewater concentrations and clinical, syndromic, and digital epidemiological data. Time-lagged cross-correlation (TLCC) was used to examine temporal dynamics among these datasets and identify the earliest emerging data for each disease and time lags. Extensive literature studies were conducted to elucidate the time-lag mechanisms for each disease, embracing the TLCC results. Random forest models were established to predict clinical cases based on WBE datasets. This was among the first studies using WBE-based approaches to identify pandemic-to-endemic transition of SARS-CoV-2. The relationships of wastewater data to traditional clinical, syndromic, and digital epidemiological surveillance data were systematically analyzed during the endemic phase of these respiratory diseases. This study demonstrates the predictive value of WBE during the endemic phase, providing early warnings and predictions for seasonal respiratory diseases, including COVID-19, influenza, and flu-like disease.

title_zh: 在呼吸道疾病流行期,废水监测Z是否具有预测价值?基于底特律市临床、废水和数字搜索数据的分析
source_body_en: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has emerged as a major public health innovation catalyzed by the COVID-19 pandemic. However, its potential remains underexplored during and after COVID-19’s transition to endemicity. This study evaluates WBE’s potential to identify the COVID-19 pandemic-to-endemic transition and to provide early warnings across multiple surveillance systems for influenza A (IAV) and B (IBV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 in the postpandemic era. We monitored SARS-CoV-2 N1 concentrations in wastewater from April 8, 2020, and July 31, 2025, generating the earliest and longest-running wastewater dataset in Detroit, MI. A peak identification method was implemented to identify the pandemic-to-endemic transition by comparing the frequency of N1 concentration peaks between phases. During the endemic phase, from October 1, 2022, and March 31, 2025, we monitored RSV, IAV, IBV, and SARS-CoV-2 in Detroit’s wastewater. Pearson correlations were implemented to quantify the associations between wastewater concentrations and clinical, syndromic, and digital epidemiological data. Time-lagged cross-correlation (TLCC) was used to examine temporal dynamics among these datasets and identify the earliest emerging data for each disease and time lags. Extensive literature studies were conducted to elucidate the time-lag mechanisms for each disease, embracing the TLCC results. Random forest models were established to predict clinical cases based on WBE datasets. This was among the first studies using WBE-based approaches to identify pandemic-to-endemic transition of SARS-CoV-2. The relationships of wastewater data to traditional clinical, syndromic, and digital epidemiological surveillance data were systematically analyzed during the endemic phase of these respiratory diseases. This study demonstrates the predictive value of WBE during the endemic phase, providing early warnings and predictions for seasonal respiratory diseases, including COVID-19, influenza, and flu-like disease.

title: From Evidence to Implementation: The Added Value of Health Economics for RSV Immunisation Implementation in Low- and Middle-Income Countries
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory infections in young children. In 2019, RSV was estimated to cause approximately 33 million acute lower respiratory infections, 3.6 million hospitalisations and more than 101,000 deaths among children under five years of age, with more than 97% of deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). The recent availability of a maternal RSV vaccine and long-acting monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) provides new opportunities to prevent severe disease during early infancy. This thesis investigates how epidemiological and health economic evidence can support the implementation of RSV immunisation strategies, with particular emphasis on LMICs. Epidemiological studies first examined RSV burden, seasonality and the age distribution of severe disease. In the Netherlands, RSV circulation was substantially disrupted during the COVID-19 pandemic, including an unusual summer epidemic in 2021, but subsequently returned towards its pre-pandemic winter pattern. Severe disease remained concentrated in young infants. Importantly, 6% of RSV-related hospitalisations among infants aged <1 year occurred within the first 14 days of life, highlighting the importance of timely protection after birth. The RSV GOLD III–ICU Network Study subsequently investigated severe respiratory infections among children aged <2 years across ten LMICs. During local RSV seasons, 29.0% of children admitted with severe respiratory illness tested positive for RSV. Most life-threatening RSV infections occurred among infants aged <6 months, with almost half occurring during the first three months of life, demonstrating the potential for early-life immunisation to prevent severe disease. Cost-of-illness studies in Mozambique and Nepal demonstrated that RSV also imposes a substantial economic burden. In Mozambique, mean costs increased from USD 612 for severe hospitalised disease to USD 1,161 for life-threatening disease requiring intensive care. Household costs represented approximately 43–145% of the monthly minimum wage. In Nepal, mean total costs were USD 312 for hospitalised cases and USD 664 for intensive-care cases, with substantial out-of-pocket expenditure relative to the monthly minimum wage. Cost-effectiveness analyses evaluated maternal vaccination and long-acting mAbs over 2025–2034. In Nepal, maternal vaccination at USD 5 per dose was estimated to prevent approximately 2,500 deaths and 50,000 hospitalisations, with an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of USD 387 per disability-adjusted life year (DALY) averted. A mAb at the same price could prevent approximately 2,400 deaths and 54,000 hospitalisations at USD 486 per DALY averted. Seasonal delivery could further improve dose efficiency. Analyses in Mozambique similarly demonstrated substantial potential health gains, although cost-effectiveness remained strongly dependent on intervention price and the cost-effectiveness threshold used. Overall, this thesis demonstrates that new RSV immunisation strategies could substantially reduce clinical and economic burden, but their value and feasibility are context-dependent. Integrating local epidemiology, healthcare utilisation, costs and implementation characteristics into economic evaluations can make estimates more relevant for national decision-making. Health economic evidence can thereby support priority setting and resource allocation, while successful and equitable implementation ultimately also depends on affordable pricing, sustainable financing and health-system readiness.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study examined RSV burden, seasonality, and the age distribution of severe disease in infants. It also included a multinational study across ten LMICs to assess severe respiratory infections in children under two years of age.
analysis.methods: Epidemiological studies were conducted to examine RSV burden, seasonality, and age distribution of severe disease. Cost-of-illness studies and cost-effectiveness analyses were performed in Mozambique and Nepal to evaluate the economic impact and feasibility of immunisation strategies.
analysis.main_results: In the Netherlands, RSV circulation was disrupted during the COVID-19 pandemic, with an unusual summer epidemic in 2021. In ten LMICs, 29.0% of children admitted with severe respiratory illness tested positive for RSV. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the potential for early-life immunisation to prevent severe disease, as most life-threatening RSV infections occurred among infants under six months of age. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Health economic evidence can support priority setting and resource allocation for RSV immunisation strategies in LMICs. analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only evidence, which may limit the depth of analysis. analysis.summary_en: This thesis explores the role of health economics in supporting the implementation of RSV immunisation strategies, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. It highlights the substantial burden of RSV in young children, with severe disease concentrated in infants under six months. Cost-of-illness studies in Mozambique and Nepal reveal significant economic impacts, while cost-effectiveness analyses suggest that maternal vaccination and monoclonal antibodies could prevent thousands of deaths and hospitalisations. The study underscores the importance of integrating local epidemiological and economic data into health evaluations to inform national decision-making. However, the findings are based on abstract-only evidence, and the cost-effectiveness of interventions depends on pricing and thresholds, which may limit their generalisability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是导致婴幼儿急性下呼吸道感染的主要原因之一。本论文探讨了流行病学和健康经济学证据如何支持RSV免疫策略的实施,特别强调了低收入和中等收入国家(LMICs)的情况。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究评估了婴儿中RSV的负担、季节性和严重疾病的年龄分布。它还包括一项跨国研究,覆盖十个LMICs,以评估<2岁儿童的严重呼吸道感染情况。
elements_zh.methods: 进行了流行病学研究以评估RSV的负担、季节性和严重疾病的年龄分布。在莫桑比克和尼泊尔进行了成本-疾病研究和成本效益分析,以评估免疫策略的经济影响和可行性。
elements_zh.main_results: In the Netherlands, RSV circulation was disrupted during the COVID-19 pandemic, with an unusual summer epidemic in 2021. In ten LMICs, 29.0% of children admitted with severe respiratory illness tested positive for RSV. Cost-of-illness studies in Mozambique and Nepal showed substantial economic burden, with mean costs increasing from USD 612 for severe hospitalised disease to USD 1,161 for life-threatening disease requiring intensive care.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现突显了早期生命免疫在预防严重疾病方面的潜力,因为大多数危及生命的RSV感染发生在<6个月的婴儿中。本研究表明,将本地RSV数据和经济数据整合到健康经济学评估中,可以提高其对国家决策的相关性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 健康经济学证据可以支持低收入和中等收入国家(LMICs)RSV免疫策略的优先事项设定和资源分配。研究结果强调了可负担的价格、可持续的融资和卫生系统准备对于成功实施的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于摘要证据,这可能限制分析的深度。干预的成本效益高度依赖于价格和阈值,研究结果的普遍性可能受到所研究国家特定背景的限制。

Cost-of-illness studies in Mozambique and Nepal demonstrated that RSV also imposes a substantial economic burden. In Mozambique, mean costs increased from USD 612 for severe hospitalised disease to USD 1,161 for life-threatening disease requiring intensive care. Household costs represented approximately 43–145% of the monthly minimum wage. In Nepal, mean total costs were USD 312 for hospitalised cases and USD 664 for intensive-care cases, with substantial out-of-pocket expenditure relative to the monthly minimum wage. Cost-effectiveness analyses evaluated maternal vaccination and long-acting mAbs over 2025–2034. In Nepal, maternal vaccination at USD 5 per dose was estimated to prevent approximately 2,500 deaths and 50,000 hospitalisations, with an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of USD 387 per disability-adjusted life year (DALY) averted. A mAb at the same price could prevent approximately 2,400 deaths and 54,000 hospitalisations at USD 486 per DALY averted. Seasonal delivery could further improve dose efficiency. Analyses in Mozambique similarly demonstrated substantial potential health gains, although cost-effectiveness remained strongly dependent on intervention price and the cost-effectiveness threshold used. Overall, this thesis demonstrates that new RSV immunisation strategies could substantially reduce clinical and economic burden, but their value and feasibility are context-dependent. Integrating local epidemiology, healthcare utilisation, costs and implementation characteristics into economic evaluations can make estimates more relevant for national decision-making. Health economic evidence can thereby support priority setting and resource allocation, while successful and equitable implementation ultimately also depends on affordable pricing, sustainable financing and health-system readiness.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是导致婴幼儿急性下呼吸道感染的主要原因之一。本论文探讨了流行病学和健康经济学证据如何支持RSV免疫策略的实施,特别强调了低收入和中等收入国家(LMICs)的情况。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究评估了婴儿中RSV的负担、季节性和严重疾病的年龄分布。它还包括一项跨国研究,覆盖十个LMICs,以评估<2岁儿童的严重呼吸道感染情况。
analysis_zh.methods: 进行了流行病学研究以评估RSV的负担、季节性和严重疾病的年龄分布。在莫桑比克和尼泊尔进行了成本-疾病研究和成本效益分析,以评估免疫策略的经济影响和可行性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现突显了早期生命免疫在预防严重疾病方面的潜力,因为大多数危及生命的RSV感染发生在<6个月的婴儿中。本研究表明,将本地RSV数据和经济数据整合到健康经济学评估中,可以提高其对国家决策的相关性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 健康经济学证据可以支持低收入和中等收入国家(LMICs)RSV免疫策略的优先事项设定和资源分配。研究结果强调了可负担的价格、可持续的融资和卫生系统准备对于成功实施的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于摘要证据,这可能限制分析的深度。干预的成本效益高度依赖于价格和阈值,研究结果的普遍性可能受到所研究国家特定背景的限制。

3Department of Pediatrics, Hospital General de México Dr. Eduardo Liceaga, Mexico City; 4Research Unit for Evidence Analysis and Synthesis, Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social, Mexico City; 5Department of Infectious Diseases, Hospital Infantil de México Federico Gómez, Mexico City;
