title_original: Age-related heterogeneity in diagnosis-coded pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae-associated hospitalizations and PICU-associated care: a single-center retrospective study

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate age-related differences in diagnosis-coded hospitalizations associated with Mycoplasma pneumoniae and the burden of PICU-associated care in pediatric patients. This is important due to the potential variability in clinical manifestations and outcomes across different age groups.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A single-center retrospective study was conducted using diagnosis-coded discharge records from a tertiary maternal and child health hospital in Hubei, China. The analytic dataset included 33,047 pediatric hospitalization records aged ≥29 days and <18 years, with 872 records associated with PICU care.
analysis.methods: The study used a de-identified structured inpatient discharge dataset and conducted a stratified systematic chart-validation substudy of 762 records to evaluate key discharge-coded variables. Logistic regression models were employed to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for PICU-associated hospitalization, with the parsimonious model including age group, sex, and selected pathogen-related coded co-diagnoses.
analysis.main_results: In 2023, monthly records of M. pneumoniae-associated hospitalizations increased from 99 in January and 139 in February to 2,282 in November. Respiratory failure/hypoxemia was recorded in 6.6% of the 1–<12 mo group versus 1.3% of the 72–<144 mo group; coded sepsis/septicemia in 11.2% versus 5.9%; and cardiac abnormality/coded myocardial involvement in 25.0% versus 15.6%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight age-related heterogeneity in diagnosis-coded phenotypes and PICU-associated burden, suggesting that younger children have a higher likelihood of severe clinical manifestations compared to older age groups. This provides novel insights into the clinical patterns of M. pneumoniae-associated hospitalizations across different pediatric age strata.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results can inform targeted surveillance and clinical management strategies for pediatric M. pneumoniae infections, particularly in younger age groups who show a higher risk of PICU-associated care. They may also guide resource allocation and early intervention protocols in hospital settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on diagnosis-coded records, which may lack specificity compared to laboratory-confirmed cases. The evidence is moderate, as it reflects hospital-based patterns rather than population incidence, and the findings are limited to a single-center retrospective analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated age-related differences in diagnosis-coded hospitalizations associated with Mycoplasma pneumoniae and the burden of PICU-associated care in pediatric patients at a tertiary maternal and child health hospital in Hubei, China. A retrospective design was used, with a stratified chart-validation subset of 762 records to evaluate key variables. The analytic dataset included 33,047 eligible pediatric hospitalizations, of which 872 were PICU-associated. Results showed a significant increase in monthly hospitalization records in 2023, peaking in November. Age-stratified analysis revealed higher rates of severe clinical manifestations, such as respiratory failure/hypoxemia, coded sepsis/septicemia, and cardiac abnormality, in younger children compared to older age groups. The findings highlight the need for age-specific clinical management and surveillance strategies for M. pneumoniae infections. However, the study is limited to diagnosis-coded data, which may lack precision, and is based on a single-center retrospective design, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨与诊断编码相关的肺炎支原体相关住院在不同年龄组中的差异,以及儿科患者与PICU相关的护理负担。由于不同年龄组在临床表现和结果上可能存在差异,因此这一研究具有重要意义。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用湖北省某三级妇幼保健医院的诊断编码出院记录,开展了一项单中心回顾性研究。分析数据集包括33,047份年龄≥29天且<18岁的儿科住院记录,其中872份与PICU护理相关。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究使用了匿名化的结构化住院出院数据集,并对762份记录进行了分层系统图表验证子研究,以评估关键的出院编码变量。采用逻辑回归模型估计与PICU相关住院的调整比值比(aORs)和95%置信区间(CIs),其中简明模型包括年龄组、性别和选定的病原体相关编码合并诊断。
elements_zh.main_results: 2023年,肺炎支原体相关住院的月记录从1月的99例和2月的139例增加到11月的2,282例。1–<12月龄组记录了6.6%的呼吸衰竭/低氧血症,而72–<144月龄组为1.3%;记录了11.2%的脓毒症/败血症,而72–<144月龄组为5.9%;记录了25.0%的心脏异常/编码心肌受累,而72–<144月龄组为15.6%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果突出了诊断编码表型和与PICU相关负担在不同年龄组中的异质性,表明年幼儿童比年长年龄组更有可能出现严重的临床表现。这为不同儿科年龄分层中肺炎支原体相关住院的临床模式提供了新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可以为针对儿科肺炎支原体感染的监测和临床管理策略提供信息,特别是对那些表现出更高PICU相关护理风险的年轻年龄组。它们也可能指导医院环境中的资源分配和早期干预协议。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于诊断编码记录,可能缺乏与实验室确认病例相比的特异性。证据强度中等,因为其反映了医院内的模式,而非人群发病率,且研究结果仅限于单中心回顾性分析。

full_text: ObjectiveDistinguishing lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) from noninfectious pulmonary infiltrates (NPIs) in patients with lymphoma is challenging. We assessed the diagnostic value of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) cytokine and lymphocyte profiles (CPs and LPs).MethodsThis retrospective study included 147 participants: 55 lymphoma patients with LRTIs, 52 with NPIs, and 40 non-lymphoma patients with LRTIs. Fourteen BALF cytokines and ten BALF and peripheral blood lymphocyte measures were assessed by multiparameter flow cytometry. LASSO-selected logistic regression models were developed using five-fold cross-validation. BALF models incorporated CPs and LPs, whereas Base models used routine inflammatory markers, with or without sputum production. Models were compared using DeLong tests, NRI, IDI, and 1,000-resample bootstrap optimism correction.ResultsLASSO retained BALF IL-8 and CD3 + CD4 + for BALF models and CRP and SAA for Base models. Test-set AUCs were 0.845 and 0.853 for BALF-A and BALF-B, vs. 0.973 and 0.969 for Base-A and Base-B, respectively. Base models significantly outperformed corresponding BALF models. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.872 for both BALF models and 0.980 and 0.977 for Base-A and Base-B. Adding sputum production improved BALF-model reclassification without significantly increasing AUC and provided no benefit to Base models. Eight immune parameters differed by lymphoma status among patients with LRTIs, with additional infection-type-specific patterns.ConclusionsBALF IL-8/CD4-based models distinguished LRTIs from NPIs in patients with lymphoma, although CRP/SAA-based models performed better. BALF immune profiling may complement conventional biomarkers and reveal immune signatures associated with lymphoma status and infection type. MethodsPatient screening and enrollmentThe inclusion criteria were as follows: (1) age ≥ 18 years; (2) a clinical diagnosis of lymphoma based on the 5th edition of the WHO Classification of Haematolymphoid Tumors; (3) fulfillment of the diagnostic criteria for LRTIs as outlined by the Chinese Thoracic Society (CTS) in 2016 and 2018 (Supplementary Table S1), confirmed by at least two pulmonologists and one microbiologist; (4) provision of informed consent and voluntary participation in the study; and (5) availability of complete data on cytokine levels and lymphocyte subsets. Exclusion criteria included: (1) diagnosis of malignant solid tumors, other hematologic diseases, or autoimmune disorders; (2) history of major solid organ transplantation; and (3) diseases other than lymphoma requiring prolonged use of specific medications, including anti-TNF-α agents, anti-IL-6 agents, Cyclosporine, Tacrolimus, Azathioprine, 6-Mercaptopurine, Mycophenolate mofetil, Sirolimus, Mizoribine, and Hydroxychloroquine. This was a retrospective observational study. Demographics, symptoms, comorbidities, clinical scores, routine laboratory findings, and etiological data were reviewed through electronic medical records. The specimens were collected from patients who underwent bronchoscopy as part of routine clinical care. The protocol was approved by the Ethics Committee of Aerospace Center Hospital (approval no. 2023070) on May 9, 2023. Written informed consent was obtained retrospectively at the time of approval; for deceased or lost-to-follow-up patients, the requirement was waived by the Ethics Committee with prior anonymization and de-identification.Bronchoalveolar lavage procedure and fluid collectionBALF was collected before antibiotic therapy or 48∼72 h after discontinuing prior antibiotics. In most cases, bronchoalveolar lavage was targeted toward affected lung segments as noted on chest computed tomography and performed with 50 mL of 0.9% sterile normal saline per lavage. Usually, three lavages were performed, with greater than or equal to 30% of the total lavage fluid being retrieved through gentle suction and filtered through sterile gauze to remove mucus strands (12). We conducted etiological examination on the collected BALF, including smear staining (Gram staining, Ziehl-Neelsen staining, and Periodic-acid silver methenamine staining), cultures (for bacteria, fungi, and mycobacteria), respiratory virus PCR (for SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A, Influenza B, Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), Adenovirus, Human rhinovirus, Cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein–Barr virus (EBV), and Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP)), and metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS). The remaining BALF samples were centrifuged, and the supernatants and precipitates were separated for cytokines and lymphocyte subsets analysis, respectively. The PB samples were collected in EDTA-K2 anticoagulant tubes (≥2 mL) for lymphocyte subset analysis using anticoagulated whole blood.Measurement of cytokine and lymphocyte profilesThe concentrations of CPs in BALF, LPs in BALF, and LPs in PB were analyzed using multiparameter flow cytometry on the DxFLEX (Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, Indianapolis, IN, USA). The human custom 14-cytokine kit, which measures IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-17A, IL-17F, IL-22, TNF-α, TNF-β, and IFN-γ, was purchased from Quantobio Biotechnology (Beijing, China), and assays were conducted according to the manufacturer's protocol. All BALF samples were analyzed using bead-based multiplex flow cytometry and were diluted 1:3 prior to testing. LPs, including CD3+, CD3 + CD4+, CD3 + CD8+, CD19+, and CD16 + CD56 + in both BALF and PB, were identified using a kit from Quantobio Biotechnology, which contained fluorescently labeled antibodies: CD3-FITC, CD16 + 56-PE, CD45-PerCP-Cy5.5, CD4-PC7, CD19-APC, and CD8-APC-Cy7. All samples, along with the manufacturer's quality control products, were immediately tested to ensure the accuracy of the detection. Data analysis was subsequently performed using Kaluza software (V2.1.1).Based on LASSO analysis and logistic regression model for discriminating Lym + LRTIs and Lym + NPIsBaseline CRP, PCT, and serum amyloid A (SAA) were used to develop the Base logistic regression (LR) models, while 24 CP and LP features were evaluated for the BALF models. All variables were initially eligible for selection using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) within five-fold cross-validation. In each iteration, four folds formed the training set and the remaining fold served as the test set. To avoid information leakage, imputation parameters, feature selection, and model fitting were derived exclusively from the training data before being applied to the held-out fold. The regularization parameter λ was determined using the one-standard-error rule, and features selected in at least 80% of the folds were retained for final modeling. Fold-specific receiver operating characteristic curves and calibration plots were averaged across iterations. Discrimination and calibration were assessed separately in the training and test sets using the area under the curve (AUC) and Brier score, with 95% confidence intervals. Additional performance measures included accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, F1 score, and Cohen's kappa. Finally, the retained predictors were refitted using the full dataset to derive the Base and BALF models, expressed aslogit(P)=β0+β1X1+⋯+βkXk.Comparison and bootstrap optimism correction of the BALF and Base modelsThe Base and BALF models were compared using differences in AUC (ΔAUC), with statistical significance assessed by the paired DeLong test. Improvements in risk prediction were further evaluated using the net reclassification improvement (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), with 95% CIs. Bootstrap internal validation with 1,000 resamples was used to estimate and correct for optimism. In each bootstrap sample, which was the same size as the original dataset and drawn with replacement, the complete modeling pipeline—including missing-data handling, feature selection, and logistic regression fitting—was repeated. Each fitted model was evaluated in both the bootstrap sample and the original dataset. For the bth iteration, optimism in the AUC was calculated asOptimismb=AUCbootstrap,b−AUCoriginal,b.The optimism-corrected AUC was then calculated asAUCcorrected=AUCapparent−11000∑b=11000⁡Optimismb.Calibration intercepts and slopes were corrected analogously.Assessment of differences in cytokine and lymphocyte profiles according to lymphoma status and infection type (viral-only vs. bacterial-only)Univariate analysis was performed to compare CPs and LPs between the Lym + LRTIs and non-Lym + LRTIs cohorts and between viral-only and bacterial-only infections. Four subgroup comparisons were conducted: Lym + viral-only LRTIs vs. Lym + bacterial-only LRTIs, Lym + viral-only LRTIs vs. non-Lym + viral-only LRTIs, Lym + bacterial-only LRTIs vs. non-Lym + bacterial-only LRTIs, and non-Lym + viral-only LRTIs vs. non-Lym + bacterial-only LRTIs. Etiology was classified at the patient level. Two pulmonologists independently reviewed microbiological results, clinical features, chest imaging, pathogen burden, potential copathogens, and treatment response while blinded to CPs and LPs results. Organisms were categorized as causative, possibly causative, colonization, contamination, or viral shedding/reactivation; disagreements were adjudicated by a microbiologist. Viral-only LRTIs required a causative virus without causative bacterial, fungal, Mycoplasma, or Chlamydia pathogens; bacterial-only LRTIs were defined similarly. Multiple causative organisms within one pathogen class remained in that category, whereas organisms from at least two classes indicated mixed infection. CMV or EBV detected by PCR or mNGS was considered causative only with compatible clinical and radiographic findings; otherwise, it was classified as reactivation or asymptomatic shedding and excluded from the viral category.Statistical analysisThe normality of continuous variables was assessed using the Shapiro–Wilk test. Continuous variables were summarized as medians with interquartile ranges (IQRs) and compared using the Mann–Whitney U test. Categorical data were presented as numbers (%), and were analyzed using either the chi-square test or Fisher's exact test. Statistical significance was defined as a two-sided P value less than 0.05. The statistical calculations and chart creation were performed using GraphPad Prism version 10 and Python version 3.13. The study workflow is presented in Figure 1, and the study was reported in accordance with the TRIPOD guidelines (13).Figure 1Flow chart of this study. This study initially enrolled 166 participants, of which 19 were excluded for failing to complete 14 cytokines and 10 lymphocytes testing. Finally, 147 cases were included in the study, consisting of 55 Lym + LRTIs, 52 Lym + NPIs, and 40 non-Lym + LRTIs. The primary analysis compared Lym + LRTIs with Lym + NPIs. Candidate features were selected using LASSO. Logistic regression (LR) models were subsequently developed and validated using five-fold cross-validation, including Base models (CRP and SAA, with or without sputum production) and BALF models. Model performance was evaluated using ROC curves with AUC, calibration plots with Brier score, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, F1 score, and Kappa. Model comparisons were performed using ΔAUC with the DeLong test, NRI, and IDI. Bootstrap optimism correction was applied to estimate the optimism-corrected AUC, calibration slope, and calibration intercept. The secondary analysis compared Lym + LRTIs with non-Lym + LRTIs using univariate analysis of CPs and LPs, followed by subgroup comparisons: viral-only vs. bacterial-only LRTIs within each lymphoma-status group, and Lym + vs. non-Lym + patients within each infection category.Flowchart showing the study design for screening 166 patients, excluding 19 due to incomplete testing, then dividing them into three cohorts: Lym+LRTIs (55), Lym+NPIs (52), and non-Lym+LRTIs (40). Describes BALF collection and flow cytometry timeline, followed by primary and secondary analyses, detailing logistic regression models, feature selection, evaluation metrics, and various group comparisons for LRTIs and NPIs. Patient screening and enrollmentThe inclusion criteria were as follows: (1) age ≥ 18 years; (2) a clinical diagnosis of lymphoma based on the 5th edition of the WHO Classification of Haematolymphoid Tumors; (3) fulfillment of the diagnostic criteria for LRTIs as outlined by the Chinese Thoracic Society (CTS) in 2016 and 2018 (Supplementary Table S1), confirmed by at least two pulmonologists and one microbiologist; (4) provision of informed consent and voluntary participation in the study; and (5) availability of complete data on cytokine levels and lymphocyte subsets. Exclusion criteria included: (1) diagnosis of malignant solid tumors, other hematologic diseases, or autoimmune disorders; (2) history of major solid organ transplantation; and (3) diseases other than lymphoma requiring prolonged use of specific medications, including anti-TNF-α agents, anti-IL-6 agents, Cyclosporine, Tacrolimus, Azathioprine, 6-Mercaptopurine, Mycophenolate mofetil, Sirolimus, Mizoribine, and Hydroxychloroquine. This was a retrospective observational study. Demographics, symptoms, comorbidities, clinical scores, routine laboratory findings, and etiological data were reviewed through electronic medical records. The specimens were collected from patients who underwent bronchoscopy as part of routine clinical care. The protocol was approved by the Ethics Committee of Aerospace Center Hospital (approval no. 2023070) on May 9, 2023. Written informed consent was obtained retrospectively at the time of approval; for deceased or lost-to-follow-up patients, the requirement was waived by the Ethics Committee with prior anonymization and de-identification. Candidate features and logistic regression models for differentiating LRTIs from NPIs in patients with lymphomaIn the five-fold cross-validation comparing the Lym + LRTIs and Lym + NPIs cohorts, missing values for CRP, PCT, and SAA were imputed using the median calculated from the corresponding training fold, and the same median was subsequently applied to the held-out test fold. LASSO analysis selected BALF_IL-8, CRP, and SAA in all five iterations, BALF_CD3 + CD4 + in four iterations, and BALF_IL-22 in three iterations; BALF_IL-5, BALF_IFN-γ, BALF_CD3 + CD8+, PB_CD3 + CD4+, and PB_CD3 + CD8 + were each selected twice, while BALF_IL-4, BALF_IL-12p70, BALF_IL-17F, BALF_CD3+, PB_CD16 + CD56+, and PCT were each selected only once, and the remaining features were never selected (Figure 2A). Ultimately, BALF_IL-8 and BALF_CD3 + CD4 + were retained as candidate features for the BALF models, whereas CRP and SAA were retained as candidate features for the Base models. Accordingly, four LR models were developed: BALF-A, which included BALF_IL-8 and BALF_CD3 + CD4+; and BALF-B, which incorporated sputum production (a clinical symptom that showed a statistically significant association) in addition to the BALF-A features; Base-A, which included CRP and SAA; Base-B, which incorporated SP in addition to the Base-A features. The four LR models demonstrated good discriminatory performance, with test-set AUCs ranging from 0.845 to 0.973; however, the Base models showed superior overall performance (Figure 2B). The calibration plots generally aligned closely with the ideal line (y = x), and the test-set Brier scores ranged from 0.053 to 0.167, with the Base models again demonstrating better performance (Figure 2B). Based on the test-set performance metrics, BALF-B slightly outperformed BALF-A, achieving a higher AUC (0.853 vs. 0.845), a lower Brier score (0.151 vs. 0.167), and higher accuracy (0.804 vs. 0.766) and F1 score (0.802 vs. 0.787) (Figure 2C). Among the Base models, Base-A achieved a slightly higher test-set AUC (0.973 vs. 0.969) and a lower Brier score (0.053 vs. 0.059) than Base-B. Predictors with nonzero coefficients at the fold-specific λ_1SE were selected. (B) ROC curves with AUC and calibration plots with Brier score of the four logistic regression models in both train and test sets. (C) The performance metrics included accuracy, sensitivity (recall), specificity, positive predictive value (PPV; precision), negative predictive value (NPV), F1 score, and Cohen's kappa of the BALF-A_Train Set, BALF-B_Train Set, Base-A_Train Set, Base-B_Train Set, BALF-A_Test Set, BALF-B_Test Set, Base-A_Test Set, Base-B_Test Set, respectively. Panel B shows ROC curves and calibration plots for training and test sets evaluating model performance. Panel C presents eight radar charts visualizing accuracy, F1-score, specificity, sensitivity, Cohen’s kappa, NPV, and PPV for different models in training and test datasets. Panel D lists model features with corresponding sample size, p-values, odds ratios, and 95% confidence intervals alongside a forest plot. full_text_sections.discussion: DiscussionIn this retrospective study of 147 patients, we developed and internally validated LR models based on BALF CPs and LPs to distinguish LRTIs from NPIs in patients with lymphoma. Several findings warrant emphasis. First, a parsimonious BALF model comprising IL-8, CD3 + CD4+ T cells, and sputum production achieved good discrimination, with a test-set AUC of 0.853 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.872 after 1,000-bootstrap validation. Second, although adding sputum production to the BALF model did not significantly improve the AUC (P = 0.791), it significantly improved risk reclassification (NRI = 0.666, 95% CI: 0.316∼0.976). Third, models based on routine inflammatory markers (CRP and SAA) significantly outperformed the BALF models (optimism-corrected AUCs of 0.977∼0.980; DeLong P < 0.01) and were considerably more robust to overfitting.The selection of IL-8 is biologically plausible. Previous research in patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma showed that IL-8 and other cytokines were elevated during respiratory bacterial infections (2). Single-cell analyses have also linked increased pulmonary CXCL8 expression to neutrophil accumulation and lung injury in severe viral and bacterial pneumonia (11, 14). These findings support BALF IL-8 as a marker of local infectious inflammation. In the lower respiratory tract, alveolar macrophages are major producers of IL-8, although type II pneumocytes, fibroblasts, and endothelial cells also contribute (15). IL-8 promotes adhesion-molecule expression and recruits neutrophils—key defenders against bacterial and fungal pathogens—into infected lung tissue (16). Binding to CXCR1 and CXCR2 further activates neutrophil metabolic and morphological responses (17). These mechanisms may explain elevated BALF IL-8 levels in patients with LRTIs and underscore its role in pulmonary host defense. Conversely, higher BALF CD3 + CD4 + proportions were associated with lower odds of LRTIs (odds ratio 0.968∼0.972 per percentage point), suggesting that preserved local T-cell immunity protects against infection. This notion is consistent with the central role of CD4+ T cells in pulmonary host defense against bacterial, viral, and fungal pathogens (18) and, conversely, with the increased susceptibility to LRTIs imposed by lymphoma and antineoplastic treatment. One additional point requires separate clarification. Lymphoma subtype distributions differed between the Lym + LRTIs and Lym + NPIs cohorts (Table 1, P = 0.004). In a sensitivity analysis restricted to B-NHL, IL-8 remained significantly different between groups (P < 0.001), whereas BALF CD3 + CD4 + did not (P = 0.180). Thus, although the IL-8 signal was robust, the overall IL-8/CD4/sputum production model as a whole should be viewed as a classifier derived from a subtype-imbalanced cohort.An important and perhaps unexpected finding was that the Base models significantly outperformed the BALF models. Several explanations should be considered. First, CRP and SAA are potent acute-phase reactants reflecting large, systemic responses, whereas BALF cytokines are local signals susceptible to lavage dilution, variable fluid recovery, and the focal distribution of infiltrates. Second, the BALF models showed greater overfitting (corrected calibration slopes 0.50∼0.53 vs. 0.71∼0.77 for the Base models); with only 107 patients, parsimonious two-variable models are inherently more stable. We therefore emphasize that the BALF model is not intended to replace routine inflammatory markers, which remain accurate, inexpensive, and universally available (19). Its potential value may instead lie in patients with atypical presentations or discordant clinical, radiological, microbiological, and systemic inflammatory findings (20).Adding sputum production to the BALF model significantly improved the NRI but did not significantly increase the AUC, while the IDI improvement was borderline. This suggests that sputum production may alter the ranking of individual predictions without materially improving overall discrimination. NRI findings should be interpreted cautiously because they are sensitive to model calibration and the definition of clinically meaningful risk categories (21). Conversely, sputum production conferred no benefit to the Base model, possibly because its diagnostic information was already captured by CRP and SAA. Future studies should evaluate incremental predictors using prespecified probability thresholds and decision-curve analysis.The secondary analysis revealed differences in BALF IL-6, IL-8, IFN-γ, and several T-, B-, and NK-cell subsets between patients with and without lymphoma who had LRTIs, as well as infection type-specific variations. Collectively, these findings suggest that lymphoma and its treatment may reshape the pulmonary immune milieu during infection (14). Nevertheless, the results should be considered exploratory because the viral-only and bacterial-only subgroups were small and multiple immune parameters were tested without adjustment for multiple comparisons. SARS-CoV-2 was the most frequently detected pathogen, accounting for 23.2% of LRTIs, consistent with enrollment overlapping the Omicron era in China. This temporal context should be considered when generalizing our findings to other periods and settings.Several limitations should be acknowledged. This retrospective, single-center study included a modest number of patients who underwent bronchoscopy, potentially introducing selection bias. Internal validation cannot replace independent prospective validation. Moreover, heterogeneity in lymphoma subtype and treatment may have confounded the observed BALF associations, while variations in BALF dilution, sampling site, and timing relative to antimicrobial therapy may have influenced biomarker concentrations.
full_text_sections.conclusion: ConclusionA BALF cytokine-lymphocyte profile-based model incorporating IL-8, CD3 + CD4+, and sputum production accurately distinguished LRTIs from NPIs in patients with lymphoma, although the model based on routine inflammatory markers (CRP and SAA) performed significantly better. BALF immune profiling may therefore complement conventional biomarkers and reveal distinct local immune signatures associated with lymphoma status and infection type. External validation is required before clinical implementation.
full_text_sections.other: IntroductionLymphoma, a malignancy arising from lymphocytes, is frequently complicated by infection. Lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) are particularly common in patients with lymphoma, largely because of disease- and treatment-related immunosuppression (1). Prompt recognition and management are essential, as severe infections may cause additional complications and increase mortality risk (2). However, diagnosing LRTIs in patients with lymphoma remains challenging for two main reasons (3). First, high-resolution computed tomography findings of chemotherapy-induced lung injury often overlap with those of LRTIs, and mixed infections further complicate etiological diagnosis. Second, conventional cultures of respiratory specimens detect a limited pathogen range, with slow turnaround and low sensitivity. Moreover, immunosuppression may cause infected lymphoma patients to present with mild or absent fever and normal serum inflammatory markers, further obscuring diagnosis (4). Lymphoma and its treatment may also alter systemic and pulmonary immune-cell profiles; characterizing these alterations could improve our understanding of immune dysregulation in patients with lymphoma and LRTIs.Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF), sampled directly from the affected pulmonary segment, reflects local inflammatory and immune responses within the lung. Compared with sputum, BALF provides a more direct assessment of the pulmonary microenvironment, particularly when clinical and radiological findings are insufficient for a definitive diagnosis. Analysis of its cellular and particulate components, including resident and recruited immune cells, together with soluble constituents such as immunoglobulins, enzymes, and antimicrobial peptides and proteins, provides deeper insight into the local immune milieu and may help distinguish LRTIs from noninfectious pulmonary infiltrates (NPIs) (5, 6).In recent years, cytokine profiles (CPs) and lymphocyte profiles (LPs) have emerged as potential biomarkers of infection (7). In lymphoma patients, conventional inflammatory markers remain valuable because they are widely available, routinely measured, and often distinguish infectious from noninfectious conditions. However, they mainly reflect systemic inflammatory burden and offer limited insight into immune mechanisms. CPs and LPs may provide complementary diagnostic information, especially in atypical presentations. More importantly, many cytokines and T-cell subsets are directly involved in LRTIs pathogenesis (8), so they may better reflect disease pathophysiology and represent potential therapeutic targets (9). A distinct BALF signature comprising elevated IL-8 and IL-13 and increased neutrophils distinguished nontuberculous mycobacterial pulmonary disease from noninfectious granulomatous lung disorders (10). In non-Hodgkin lymphoma, IL-6 and IL-8 outperformed fever, procalcitonin (PCT), and CRP for early detection of respiratory bacterial infection, particularly in minimally symptomatic patients (2). Moreover, single-cell transcriptomics identified a CXCL8 (IL-8)-neutrophil recruitment axis as a key determinant of pneumonia severity (11).Previous studies have primarily focused on analyzing CPs and LPs in peripheral blood (PB) for LRTIs diagnosis. However, lower respiratory tract specimens obtained directly from the infection site offer distinct advantages in differentiating LRTIs, making the analysis of CPs and LPs in BALF essential. Our analyses addressed two distinct clinical and biological questions. The primary analysis compared lymphoma patients with LRTIs (Lym + LRTIs) versus those with noninfectious pulmonary infiltrates (Lym + NPIs), thereby addressing a clinically relevant differential diagnosis in lymphoma patients presenting with pulmonary infiltrates, in whom infectious and noninfectious etiologies must be distinguished. In contrast, the secondary analysis focused on patients with confirmed LRTIs and compared pulmonary immune profiles according to lymphoma status. Usually, three lavages were performed, with greater than or equal to 30% of the total lavage fluid being retrieved through gentle suction and filtered through sterile gauze to remove mucus strands (12). We conducted etiological examination on the collected BALF, including smear staining (Gram staining, Ziehl-Neelsen staining, and Periodic-acid silver methenamine staining), cultures (for bacteria, fungi, and mycobacteria), respiratory virus PCR (for SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A, Influenza B, Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), Adenovirus, Human rhinovirus, Cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein–Barr virus (EBV), and Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP)), and metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS). The remaining BALF samples were centrifuged, and the supernatants and precipitates were separated for cytokines and lymphocyte subsets analysis, respectively. The PB samples were collected in EDTA-K2 anticoagulant tubes (≥2 mL) for lymphocyte subset analysis using anticoagulated whole blood. title_original: Diagnostic value of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cytokine and lymphocyte profiles for lower respiratory tract infections in patients with lymphoma

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic utility of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) cytokine and lymphocyte profiles for lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) in patients with lymphoma, addressing the need for improved diagnostic tools in this vulnerable population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective study included 147 participants: 55 lymphoma patients with LRTIs, 52 with non-pulmonary infections (NPIs), and 40 non-lymphoma patients with LRTIs. Exclusion criteria included diagnoses of malignant solid tumors, other hematologic diseases, or autoimmune disorders, as well as diseases requiring prolonged use of specific medications.

This was a retrospective observational study. Demographics, symptoms, comorbidities, clinical scores, routine laboratory findings, and etiological data were reviewed through electronic medical records. ObjectiveDistinguishing lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) from noninfectious pulmonary infiltrates (NPIs) in patients with lymphoma is challenging. abstract_zh: 我们评估了支气管肺泡灌洗液(BALF)细胞因子和淋巴细胞谱(CPs和LPs)的诊断价值。方法本回顾性研究包括147名参与者:55名淋巴瘤合并下呼吸道感染(LRTIs)的患者,52名非肺部感染(NPIs)的患者,以及40名非淋巴瘤合并LRTIs的患者。患者筛选和纳入标准纳入标准如下:(1)年龄≥18岁;(2)根据世界卫生组织(WHO)第5版血液淋巴肿瘤分类的临床诊断为淋巴瘤;(3)符合中国胸科学会(CTS)2016年和2018年制定的LRTIs诊断标准(补充表S1),由至少两名肺科医生和一名微生物学家确认;(4)签署知情同意书并自愿参与研究;(5)具备完整的细胞因子水平和淋巴细胞亚群数据。这是一项回顾性观察性研究。通过电子病历回顾了人口统计学、症状、合并症、临床评分、常规实验室检查结果和病原学数据。对收集的BALF进行了病原学检查,包括涂片染色(革兰染色、齐-尼尔森染色和过碘酸雪夫染色)、培养(细菌、真菌和分枝杆菌)、呼吸道病毒PCR(SARS-CoV-2、流感A、流感B、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)、腺病毒、人类鼻病毒、巨细胞病毒(CMV)、EB病毒(EBV)和肺炎支原体(MP)),以及宏基因组下一代测序(mNGS)。目标在淋巴瘤患者中区分下呼吸道感染(LRTIs)和非感染性肺浸润(NPIs)具有挑战性。通过多参数流式细胞术分析了14种BALF细胞因子和10种BALF及外周血淋巴细胞指标,样本在检测前稀释为1:3。病原学检查包括涂片染色、培养、呼吸道病毒PCR(SARS-CoV-2、流感A、流感B、RSV、腺病毒、人类鼻病毒、CMV、EBV和MP)以及宏基因组下一代测序(mNGS)。使用LASSO特征选择和五折交叉验证开发了逻辑回归模型,并使用训练折的中位数对缺失值进行插补。主要结果开发了四个逻辑回归模型,测试集AUC值范围为0.845至0.973。包含CRP和SAA的基线模型整体表现优于BALF模型。解释与创新性作者认为,基线模型在诊断淋巴瘤患者LRTIs方面优于BALF模型,表明传统生物标志物可能在此背景下比BALF细胞因子和淋巴细胞谱更有效。科学与公共卫生意义这些发现可能有助于为免疫功能低下患者开发更准确的LRTIs诊断策略,从而改善临床决策和治疗结果。局限性与证据强度该研究受到回顾性设计和潜在数据缺失的限制,尽管使用五折交叉验证和中位数插补增强了证据的可信度。由于这些限制,结果的可信度中等。

title: Further optimization of an ADMA Biologic's proprietary manufacturing process to ensure removal of impurities associated with thrombosis risk in IVIG products

source_records.title: Further optimization of an ADMA Biologic's proprietary manufacturing process to ensure removal of impurities associated with thrombosis risk in IVIG products
Further optimization of an ADMA Biologic's proprietary manufacturing process to ensure removal of impurities associated with thrombosis risk in IVIG products

priority_tier_reason: 补充性记录、预印本或证据完整度有限
full_text: AbstractThromboembolic events (TEEs) are a rare, but serious adverse event for patients receiving immunoglobulin therapy. Patient and product-specific risk factors can increase the risk for these adverse events. To reduce this risk, ADMA has further optimized the manufacturing process of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) products to remove impurities that may precipitate these events. Key attributes were tested in three lots of ADMA's IVIG products from the further optimized process. Across the three lots analyzed, quantification values for each parameter tested were at or below the limit. Since the commercial release of ADMA's IVIG products produced using the further optimized manufacturing process, ADMA's post-marketing pharmacovigilance surveillance and the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System has received zero reported cases of TEEs from July 1, 2025 to July 31, 2026. ADMA's further optimized manufacturing process ensures removal of impurities while also ensuring high recovery of immunoglobulin from source material.Keywords: Factor XIa, immunoglobulin, primary immunodeficiency, safety, thrombosis 2.Methods2.1.ManufacturingADMA IVIG products are licensed products, approved by the FDA and meet requirements for IVIG products. These products are manufactured by a modified Cohn-Oncley fractionation method. The details of ADMA Biologics’ manufacturing process for IVIG products have been previously reported with the systematic quality by design optimization after acquisition of the manufacturing plant from Biotest (4). This process has since then been further optimized with the addition of anion and cation exchange steps for added purification, an increase to a total of six virus inactivation steps to remove or inactivate blood-borne pathogens, and yield improvements resulting in a 20% or more increase in production from the same starting plasma material.2.2.Analytical testingKey attributes related to procoagulant impurities were measured in three IVIG product lots produced using ADMA's further optimized process. These included Factor XIa, cholesterol, non-activated partial thromboplastin time (NAPTT), PKA, IgA, IgM, and chromatographic purity. Factor XIa enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was used to determine the total FXIa at key process steps and in the final product. NAPTT assay was used to assess procoagulant activity at a 1:10 dilution and followed the European Pharmacopoeia (EP) compendial method with one difference, which is the positive control, which consists of drug product spiked with FXIa to assess system and assay suitability. Cholesterol was measured using a fluorometric assay that measures total cholesterol in human plasma-derived products. PKA activity was determined by an endpoint amidolytic method. Total IgA and IgM presence were determined by ELISA. Chromatographic purity was analyzed using high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) to determine the relative amount of aggregates, dimers, monomers, and fragments. The percent yield change was assessed across 24 lots of ADMA's IVIG products.2.3.Post-marketing adverse event surveillanceCases of TEEs were searched via internal ADMA post-marketing pharmacovigilance database and public FDA adverse event reporting system (FAERS) (10). Reports were included any cases since the first commercial lots of ADMA IVIG products were available from the further optimized process, July 1 2025, to July 31, 2026 (11). Internal post-marketing pharmacovigilance search included reports under the Standardized MedDRA Query “Embolic and Thrombotic Events.” Cases from FAERs were included if they were in the United States. Cases from the literature were included if the product was distinctly mentioned. Supplementary materialThe Supplementary Material for this article can be found online at: https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fcvm.2026.1874074/full#supplementary-material Supplementary Materials 3.ResultsThree lots of ADMA's IVIG products that were manufactured using the further optimized process were analyzed. The results reported for each analytical test were from the final product. All results of the critical attributes analyzed were similar or improved in the further optimized process.3.1.Analytical testingTo assess impurities that can increase the risk for TEEs, FXIa and cholesterol were assessed. Across the three lots analyzed, two of the three had levels below the limit of quantification for FXIa, and all three lots had below the limit of quantification for cholesterol (Table 1). The results of the NAPTT assay across the three lots had an average coagulation time of 293.7 s.Table 1Results from analytical testing of impurities and bioactivity testing using non-activated partial thromboplastin time (NAPTT).AssayLot 1Lot 2Lot 3FXIa<0.91 mIU/mLa<0.91 mIU/mLa1.2 mIU/mLCholesterol<0.24 mg/dLa<0.24 mg/dLa<0.24 mg/dLaNAPTT 1:10 dilution294 s295 s292 sPKA<3 IU/mL<3 IU/mL<3 IU/mLProteolytic activity<10 U/La<10 U/La<10 U/LaIgA<43 μg/mLa<43 μg/mLa<43 μg/mLaIgM0 μg/mL0 μg/mL0 μg/mLChromatographic Purity—percent aggregates and fragments0%0%0%aLimit of quantification.Additional impurities analyzed revealed effective removal of PKA, proteolytic activity, IgA, and IgM across all three lots. Across the three lots analyzed, there was no evidence of aggregates or fragments in the final IVIG product.Assessment of yield improvement across 24 lots of ADMA's IVIG process can be seen in Figure 1. With this further optimized process, there was an approximate 20% increase in the yield utilizing the same starting plasma.Figure 1Percent change in yield measured in ADMA's IVIG lots with further optimized process.Line graph showing percent yield increase across 24 lots at the Yield Enhanced IVIG process step. Yield ranges mostly between 20 and 25 percent with minor fluctuations among lots.3.2.Post-marketing adverse event surveillanceSince the commercial release of ADMA's IVIG products produced using the further optimized manufacturing process, ADMA's post-marketing pharmacovigilance surveillance and FAERs has received zero reported cases of TEEs. 4.DiscussionThrombosis is a rare, but serious side effect of IG products, and appropriate manufacturing techniques are needed to ensure safety and quality of the products available, especially for patients with primary humoral immunodeficiency who receive these life-long therapies.Previous reports on ADMA's manufacturing process demonstrated its ability to remove procoagulant impurities (4). Analyzed lots of ADMA's IVIG products that were produced with the further optimized process yielded results that demonstrate low levels of coagulation factors, with two of the three lots having levels below the limit of quantification for Factor XIa. Additionally, cholesterol, which can also adversely impact patient health over time, was removed below quantifiable limits across all three lots. The results from this further optimized process demonstrate the robust capabilities of ADMA's manufacturing facility to produce an improved product yield while ensuring high quality and safe IVIG products.FXIa has been linked to thrombotic events in IG products, and removal of this pro-coagulant factor is vital to ensure safety (5). This has previously resulted in improved manufacturing processes, labeling changes, and even the withdrawal and re-introduction of other IG products (6). However, there are additional impurities that can increase the risk for clotting in IG products that also must be taken into consideration. Evaluating NAPTT, a measure of clotting time, allows for an encompassing approach to evaluating thrombotic risk of IG products. Previous studies have demonstrated manufacturing processes resulting in an NAPTT time of >200 s are associated with reduced TEEs (12), while recent studies have demonstrated reduced clotting factors with corresponding NAPTT times around 277 s at a 1:10 dilution (8). In this further optimized process, the average NAPTT time across the three lots at a 1:10 dilution was 293.7 s, with all three lots above 250 s indicating very low levels of procoagulant activity.ADMA's proprietary manufacturing process minimizes thermal, physical, and chemical stressors on IVIG products as previously described (4). This process has demonstrated its ability to appropriately remove impurities from source material, such as IgA, below quantifiable limits. Though rare, IgA deficient patients have experienced anaphylactic reactions when given IG products that contain moderate amounts of IgA (13). While the majority of IG products contain moderate levels of IgA, a study demonstrating that IVIG-related side effects increase with increasing levels of IgA in the various brands of IVIG has not been conducted and tolerability of individual IVIG products would appear to be dependent on other factors than IgA. Another key indicator of process and product quality in IVIG manufacturing is the quality of the IgG molecules themselves. Across the three lots of ADMA IVIG products analyzed, no aggregates or fragments were detected. This process is designed to prevent the formation of aggregates and does not necessitate additional techniques, such as vibration, to prevent or disrupt aggregation that could weaken the integrity of the IG. This demonstrates not only the sufficient removal of impurities to ensure safety but also preserved quality and integrity of ADMA's IVIG products.No TEEs have been reported since the release of commercial lots that were manufactured with ADMA's further optimized process. full_text_sections.abstract: AbstractThromboembolic events (TEEs) are a rare, but serious adverse event for patients receiving immunoglobulin therapy. Patient and product-specific risk factors can increase the risk for these adverse events. To reduce this risk, ADMA has further optimized the manufacturing process of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) products to remove impurities that may precipitate these events. Key attributes were tested in three lots of ADMA's IVIG products from the further optimized process. Across the three lots analyzed, quantification values for each parameter tested were at or below the limit. Since the commercial release of ADMA's IVIG products produced using the further optimized manufacturing process, ADMA's post-marketing pharmacovigilance surveillance and the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System has received zero reported cases of TEEs from July 1, 2025 to July 31, 2026. ADMA's further optimized manufacturing process ensures removal of impurities while also ensuring high recovery of immunoglobulin from source material.Keywords: Factor XIa, immunoglobulin, primary immunodeficiency, safety, thrombosis

full_text_sections.discussion: 4.DiscussionThrombosis is a rare, but serious side effect of IG products, and appropriate manufacturing techniques are needed to ensure safety and quality of the products available, especially for patients with primary humoral immunodeficiency who receive these life-long therapies.Previous reports on ADMA's manufacturing process demonstrated its ability to remove procoagulant impurities (4). Analyzed lots of ADMA's IVIG products that were produced with the further optimized process yielded results that demonstrate low levels of coagulation factors, with two of the three lots having levels below the limit of quantification for Factor XIa. Additionally, cholesterol, which can also adversely impact patient health over time, was removed below quantifiable limits across all three lots. The results from this further optimized process demonstrate the robust capabilities of ADMA's manufacturing facility to produce an improved product yield while ensuring high quality and safe IVIG products.FXIa has been linked to thrombotic events in IG products, and removal of this pro-coagulant factor is vital to ensure safety (5). This has previously resulted in improved manufacturing processes, labeling changes, and even the withdrawal and re-introduction of other IG products (6). However, there are additional impurities that can increase the risk for clotting in IG products that also must be taken into consideration. Evaluating NAPTT, a measure of clotting time, allows for an encompassing approach to evaluating thrombotic risk of IG products. Previous studies have demonstrated manufacturing processes resulting in an NAPTT time of >200 s are associated with reduced TEEs (12), while recent studies have demonstrated reduced clotting factors with corresponding NAPTT times around 277 s at a 1:10 dilution (8). In this further optimized process, the average NAPTT time across the three lots at a 1:10 dilution was 293.7 s, with all three lots above 250 s indicating very low levels of procoagulant activity.ADMA's proprietary manufacturing process minimizes thermal, physical, and chemical stressors on IVIG products as previously described (4). This process has demonstrated its ability to appropriately remove impurities from source material, such as IgA, below quantifiable limits. Though rare, IgA deficient patients have experienced anaphylactic reactions when given IG products that contain moderate amounts of IgA (13). While the majority of IG products contain moderate levels of IgA, a study demonstrating that IVIG-related side effects increase with increasing levels of IgA in the various brands of IVIG has not been conducted and tolerability of individual IVIG products would appear to be dependent on other factors than IgA. Another key indicator of process and product quality in IVIG manufacturing is the quality of the IgG molecules themselves. Across the three lots of ADMA IVIG products analyzed, no aggregates or fragments were detected. This process is designed to prevent the formation of aggregates and does not necessitate additional techniques, such as vibration, to prevent or disrupt aggregation that could weaken the integrity of the IG. This demonstrates not only the sufficient removal of impurities to ensure safety but also preserved quality and integrity of ADMA's IVIG products.No TEEs have been reported since the release of commercial lots that were manufactured with ADMA's further optimized process. The reports for the post-marketing surveillance is limited by the short follow-up time since the commercial release of these further optimized lots, however this provides supportive real-world context regarding these adverse events. Estimates of thrombosis related to IG products are around 1%, but this risk can vary depending on individual patient's risk factors for TEEs outside of product composition (1, 2, 6). The rarity of these adverse events taken in context with the ability of ADMA's further optimized manufacturing process to reduce impurities known to precipitate these events provides support of the capabilities of this manufacturing process to produce safe IVIG products.
full_text_sections.conclusion: 5.ConclusionADMA's further optimized manufacturing process ensures removal of impurities while also ensuring high recovery of IG from source material. The analytical testing of ADMA's IVIG products after further optimization revealed low Factor XIa and an average NAPTT 293.7 s across three lots, demonstrating that robust measures have been taken in the manufacturing process to reduce the risk of TEEs in patients on ADMA's IVIG products. This process results in IVIG products with high purity, as demonstrated in this analysis and high yield of IG from source materials, reducing the risk of leaving behind valuable antibodies to protect patients against commonly encountered pathogens. These improvements to the manufacturing process can help ensure that patients are able to reliably receive safe and efficacious IVIG products.

full_text: BackgroundFollowing the lifting of pandemic-era restrictions, China experienced a sharp resurgence in pediatric respiratory infections; however, post-pandemic epidemiological and climatic data on lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) from the temperate continental climate of northern China remain scarce.MethodsIn this retrospective, single-center surveillance study, we characterized the post-pandemic epidemiology of six respiratory viruses in children hospitalized with LRTI in Tianjin and assessed their pathogen-specific, lagged climatic associations. Children aged 0–18 years hospitalized between January 2023 and December 2025 were tested by targeted next-generation sequencing for human rhinovirus (HRV), adenovirus (ADV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human bocavirus (HBoV), influenza virus (IFV), and human metapneumovirus (HMPV). Pathogen–climate associations were estimated using a quasi-Poisson model that adjusted for seasonality, secular trend, and lagged meteorological exposures.ResultsAmong 2,597 virus-positive cases, the leading pathogens were HRV (30.7%), ADV (26.6%), and RSV (20.6%), followed by HBoV (12.1%), IFV (6.0%), and HMPV (4.0%). Age distributions differed by pathogen (p<0.05): RSV and HBoV predominated in infants and toddlers, HRV and HMPV in preschoolers, ADV in school-aged children, and IFV across the older preschool-to-school-age range; males predominated for all viruses except IFV. Five viruses peaked in December, whereas HBoV peaked uniquely in July. After adjustment for seasonality and secular trend, the unadjusted associations of IFV with humidity and temperature disappeared, indicating that they largely reflected shared seasonality. In contrast, RSV retained associations with temperature (RR 3.87, 95% CI 1.39–10.76) and wind speed (RR 5.46, 95% CI 2.39–12.47) at a 1-month lag, and HMPV with temperature (RR 13.3, 95% CI 1.64–108.3; imprecise given its low case count); HRV, ADV, and HBoV showed no independent climatic associations. Co-infections occurred in 116 cases (4.5%), most frequently HBoV+HRV (23.3%).ConclusionPost-pandemic pediatric viral LRTI in Tianjin shows distinctive pathogen-specific profiles in age, seasonality, and climatic sensitivity. The summer peak of HBoV and the seasonally independent climatic drivers of RSV and HMPV provide a preliminary basis that, if confirmed with higher-resolution data, could inform pathogen-tailored, climate-informed surveillance in northern Chinese megacities. 2Materials and methods2.1Study design, setting and populationWe conducted a retrospective single-center surveillance study at the Department of Respiratory Medicine, Tianjin Children’s Hospital (Ma-Chang campus), the only tertiary-A comprehensive children’s hospital in Tianjin. The hospital is the principal pediatric referral center for Tianjin municipality and, for selected specialties, draws patients from across the wider North China Plain; publicly reported hospital-wide figures indicate roughly 17,000–20,000 pediatric admissions per year across all departments. Our cohort of 2,597 virologically confirmed viral LRTI cases represents the subset of hospitalized LRTI cases that were both tested and found positive for one of the six target viruses, not the total burden of pediatric LRTI hospitalization in Tianjin. A precise, denominator-based estimate of the proportion of all Tianjin pediatric LRTI hospitalizations captured by this cohort is not available, because no citywide pediatric LRTI hospitalization registry exists for comparison. As a tertiary referral center, the cohort is likely enriched for more severe disease and for cases referred from primary and secondary facilities; this referral pattern, and the resulting limit on generalizability to primary care, is revisited in the Discussion (Section 4.6).Eligible participants were children aged 0–18 years hospitalized with a clinical diagnosis of LRTI between 1 January 2023 and 31 December 2025, from whom a respiratory specimen was submitted for routine viral testing. LRTI was defined clinically, following the 2019 Chinese Pediatric Society guideline for community-acquired pneumonia (Subspecialty Group of Respiratory Diseases, 2019), as cough or fever (axillary temperature ≥38 °C) together with at least one of: tachypnoea, wheezing, crackles on auscultation, or imaging evidence of pneumonia or bronchiolitis. This definition captures the clinical syndromes of pneumonia and bronchiolitis and excludes isolated upper respiratory tract infection. We excluded children with pre-existing chronic respiratory disease, congenital airway malformations, documented immunodeficiency, active malignancy, or concurrent infection by pathogens outside the predefined six-virus panel. This last criterion operated at the level of the child rather than of the laboratory result: whenever the tNGS report carried a Class A detection of a bacterial, atypical or non-panel viral pathogen alongside one of the six target viruses, the case was removed from the cohort at eligibility screening, so no such child contributes to any analysis reported here. For descriptive analyses, children were stratified a priori into four age categories: infants (<1 year), toddlers (1–2 years), preschoolers (3–5 years) and school-aged children (≥6 years). All records were de-identified before analysis. The vendor’s reporting algorithm assigned each detected organism a clinical pathogenicity grade, from Class A (highest confidence) through lower-confidence grades. The panel was introduced during 2023 and reached full clinical implementation in the fourth quarter of that year, after which testing volume remained broadly stable through 2024 and 2025. Monthly counts of tNGS requests could not be retrieved from the laboratory information system for the whole study window, so this account of testing volume rests on the laboratory’s implementation record rather than on an auditable series of test counts, and it should be read as such.The grade is a composite call rather than a single read-count cut-off. Second, restricting to Class A calls minimizes the inclusion of low-confidence or incidental detections. Third, bacterial and atypical pathogens are subject to different detection biases (for example, antibiotic pretreatment and colonization) and different climate–transmission mechanisms, and were therefore outside the scope of this analysis. Co-infections, defined as concurrent Class A detection of two or more of the six target viruses in the same specimen, were identified and are described in Section 2.4.2.3Meteorological dataMonthly city-wide meteorological summaries for Tianjin from January 2023 to December 2025 (n = 36 months) were obtained from the Tianjin Meteorological Bureau and comprised mean atmospheric pressure (hPa), mean wind speed (m/s), mean air temperature (°C), mean relative humidity (%), precipitation (mm) and mean daily sunshine duration (hours). Finer (for example, weekly) resolution would allow more precise estimation of short-lag effects and is standard in DLNM-based climate–infection studies (Gasparrini et al., 2010; Li et al., 2025); we discuss this resolution constraint further in Section 4.6.2.4Statistical analysisCategorical data are presented as counts (percentages) and compared between groups with Pearson’s χ2 test; the assumption of an equal sex ratio was tested with the exact binomial test, and inter-pathogen age differences with the Kruskal–Wallis test. Daily case records were aggregated to monthly totals and merged with the meteorological time series. Yates’ continuity correction was applied to 2 × 2 comparisons.Co-infections were tabulated separately from the mono-infection pathogen spectrum. full_text_sections.abstract: BackgroundFollowing the lifting of pandemic-era restrictions, China experienced a sharp resurgence in pediatric respiratory infections; however, post-pandemic epidemiological and climatic data on lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) from the temperate continental climate of northern China remain scarce.MethodsIn this retrospective, single-center surveillance study, we characterized the post-pandemic epidemiology of six respiratory viruses in children hospitalized with LRTI in Tianjin and assessed their pathogen-specific, lagged climatic associations. Children aged 0–18 years hospitalized between January 2023 and December 2025 were tested by targeted next-generation sequencing for human rhinovirus (HRV), adenovirus (ADV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human bocavirus (HBoV), influenza virus (IFV), and human metapneumovirus (HMPV). Pathogen–climate associations were estimated using a quasi-Poisson model that adjusted for seasonality, secular trend, and lagged meteorological exposures.ResultsAmong 2,597 virus-positive cases, the leading pathogens were HRV (30.7%), ADV (26.6%), and RSV (20.6%), followed by HBoV (12.1%), IFV (6.0%), and HMPV (4.0%). Age distributions differed by pathogen (p<0.05): RSV and HBoV predominated in infants and toddlers, HRV and HMPV in preschoolers, ADV in school-aged children, and IFV across the older preschool-to-school-age range; males predominated for all viruses except IFV. Five viruses peaked in December, whereas HBoV peaked uniquely in July. After adjustment for seasonality and secular trend, the unadjusted associations of IFV with humidity and temperature disappeared, indicating that they largely reflected shared seasonality. In contrast, RSV retained associations with temperature (RR 3.87, 95% CI 1.39–10.76) and wind speed (RR 5.46, 95% CI 2.39–12.47) at a 1-month lag, and HMPV with temperature (RR 13.3, 95% CI 1.64–108.3; imprecise given its low case count); HRV, ADV, and HBoV showed no independent climatic associations. Co-infections occurred in 116 cases (4.5%), most frequently HBoV+HRV (23.3%).ConclusionPost-pandemic pediatric viral LRTI in Tianjin shows distinctive pathogen-specific profiles in age, seasonality, and climatic sensitivity. The summer peak of HBoV and the seasonally independent climatic drivers of RSV and HMPV provide a preliminary basis that, if confirmed with higher-resolution data, could inform pathogen-tailored, climate-informed surveillance in northern Chinese megacities.

full_text_sections.results: 3Results3.1Overall pathogen distribution and demographicsAcross 36 surveillance months we identified 2,597 virologically confirmed pediatric LRTI cases. HRV was the most frequently detected virus (796 cases, 30.7%), followed by ADV (692, 26.6%), RSV (536, 20.6%), HBoV (313, 12.1%), IFV (155, 6.0%) and HMPV (105, 4.0%) (Figure 2A; Table 1). Sputum was the predominant specimen type for HRV, RSV, HBoV, HMPV and IFV. The proportion of cases sampled from the lower airway (sputum or BALF) likewise differed across pathogens (χ2 = 73.7, df = 5, p < 0.001), ranging from 70.1% for ADV and 70.5% for HMPV to 88.5% for HBoV (Table 1). ADV was more evenly distributed across specimen types, with BALF (35.4%) and sputum (34.7%) contributing similar shares and nasopharyngeal swabs a further 29.6%, giving ADV a markedly higher BALF share than the other five viruses (Figure 2B). Annual case counts rose from 188 in 2023 to 1,027 in 2024 and 1,382 in 2025 (Figure 2C). The 2023 figures warrant particular caution on this account. The assay reached full clinical implementation only in the fourth quarter of that year (Section 2.2), so the 188 cases recorded in 2023 almost certainly under-represent circulation during the early post-pandemic period relative to 2024 and 2025, when testing volume was broadly stable. Subsequent analyses therefore emphasize pathogen composition, age distribution and seasonal timing, which are far less sensitive to testing volume than absolute case counts.Figure 2Overall pathogen spectrum and specimen characteristics of pediatric viral LRTI in Tianjin, 2023–2025. (A) Case distribution across the six viral pathogens, ranked by prevalence. (B) Specimen-type composition by pathogen. (C) Annual case burden, stacked by pathogen.Grouped bar and stacked bar chart panel showing (A) case numbers and percentages for six pathogens, (B) specimen composition by pathogen, and (C) annual case burden from 2023 to 2025. HRV and ADV have the highest positive cases, sputum is the most common specimen, and total case burden increases each year, with pathogen contribution shown by color.Two features of the assay bound the influence of testing volume without removing it. All six viruses sit on a single multiplex panel and are screened simultaneously in every specimen, so no virus could be tested more often than another, and a change in ordering volume alters which children were tested rather than which viruses were sought. What this cannot exclude is a shift in case mix: if tNGS was ordered preferentially for more severely ill children, and if the pathogen spectrum of severe admissions differs from that of milder ones, composition will move with ordering practice. The markedly higher BALF share of ADV (Figure 2B) is consistent with such a gradient, and the point is developed in Section 4.6.Boys predominated for HRV (59.2%, p<0.001), ADV (61.4%, p<0.001), RSV (56.7%, p=0.002), HBoV (57.2%, p=0.013) and HMPV (62.9%, p=0.011), whereas IFV showed a balanced sex ratio (53.5% male, p=0.42) (Table 1; Figure 3A). Although IFV was the only virus without a male excess, a χ2 test for heterogeneity across the six pathogens did not reach significance (χ2 = 5.77, df = 5, p = 0.33), and neither did the comparison of IFV against the other five viruses combined (χ2 = 1.68, df = 1, p = 0.20). The balanced ratio for IFV is therefore better read as a failure to demonstrate a male excess in the smallest of the larger groups (n = 155) than as evidence of a genuinely different sex distribution.Figure 3Demographic composition of pediatric viral LRTI by pathogen. (A) Sex distribution, with binomial-test significance markers. (B) Age (years) by pathogen (median, IQR), with jittered individual data points overlaid. Significance markers: *p<0.05, **p<0.01, ***p<0.001; ns = not significant.Bar chart on the left shows male and female sex distribution for six pathogens with males consistently higher for HRV, ADV, RSV, HBoV, and HMPV; differences denoted by statistical significance symbols. Boxplot on the right displays age distribution in years for each pathogen with medians, interquartile ranges, and data points, indicating variation in median ages by pathogen.Age distributions differed sharply across pathogens (Kruskal–Wallis H = 372.7, p < 0.001; Figure 3B). Infants and toddlers carried most HBoV (median 2.0 [IQR 1.0–4.0] years) and RSV (3.0 [1.0–4.0]) cases; preschoolers were the main group for HRV (4.0 [2.0–6.0]) and HMPV (4.0 [1.8–6.0]); ADV predominated in school-aged children (6.0 [3.0–8.0]), while IFV spanned the older preschool-to-school-age range (median 5.0 [2.0–7.0]) (Table 1; Figure 3B).3.2Temporal distributionMonthly time-series of the six pathogens (Figure 4A) showed strong but pathogen-specific seasonality. HRV, ADV, RSV, IFV and HMPV all reached their annual maxima in December, consistent with the cold, dry continental winter being the dominant transmission season in northern China. The December peak of late 2024 (about 400 positive cases that month) was the largest monthly count of the surveillance period, with a smaller but still notable winter peak in December 2025. ADV showed a secondary peak in late spring (April–May), and HRV and ADV together produced the broadest seasonal envelope (March–December) of any pathogen. The seasonal heatmap (Figure 4B) summarizes these patterns: each virus shows at least one clearly defined month-of-year peak, and HBoV is the only virus to peak in a warm-season month (July). Because the heatmap is normalized row-wise, color intensity for each pathogen is scaled to its own monthly range; the visual prominence of a peak for a low-incidence pathogen (for example, HMPV) therefore does not indicate the same absolute case count as for a high-incidence pathogen (for example, HRV).Figure 4Temporal distribution of pediatric viral LRTI, 2023–2025. full_text_sections.discussion: 4DiscussionIn this three-year, single-center cohort we characterized the post-pandemic epidemiology of pediatric viral LRTI in Tianjin, a megacity on the North China Plain, and quantified how closely monthly viral activity tracks ambient weather. To our knowledge, the dataset is unusual for northern China in spanning six respiratory viruses, including the comparatively under-surveyed HRV, HBoV and HMPV, over the full 2023–2025 post-pandemic rebound window, with a complete and time-matched monthly meteorological record.4.1Principal epidemiological featuresAcross the six viruses, HRV, ADV and RSV were the leading causes of pediatric LRTI, and each pathogen carried a well-defined demographic profile. Age and sex stratification confirmed recognized biological gradients. RSV and HBoV were most prevalent in infants and toddlers, in line with airway and immune development (Feng et al., 2024; Jiang et al., 2016; Li et al., 2022); ADV peaked in school-aged children and IFV in the older preschool-to-school-age range, consistent with close-contact transmission in schools and other crowded settings (Fang et al., 2025; Yu et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2023); and HMPV showed an intermediate distribution. The older age skew of IFV fits its epidemiology in temperate regions, where school-aged children are the principal drivers of seasonal influenza transmission and the group in which symptomatic infection is most readily recognized, in contrast to the infant and toddler predominance of RSV and HBoV (Feng et al., 2024; Klein and Flanagan, 2016). The male predominance for HRV, ADV, RSV, HBoV and HMPV, but not IFV, echoes prior pediatric LRTI cohorts and may reflect sex differences in innate immunity and behavior (Klein and Flanagan, 2016). The strong age-group × pathogen association reinforces the need for an explicitly age-stratified surveillance framework.The six pathogens also fell into two distinct seasonal groups. HRV, ADV, RSV, IFV and HMPV all peaked in December, during the cold, dry continental winter, whereas HBoV stood apart with an isolated July maximum—the only warm-season peak of the panel. HRV additionally displayed the broadest seasonal envelope, circulating from March to December, consistent with fundamentally endemic, weakly seasonal behavior. Because the rise in absolute case counts partly reflects expanding testing volume rather than incidence (Section 3.1), the interpretation that follows rests on pathogen composition, age structure and seasonal timing rather than on raw counts.4.2Interpretation in the post-pandemic contextThese patterns are best read against, rather than directly measured against, pre-pandemic Chinese pediatric surveillance, since our cohort describes the post-pandemic period without a matched pre-pandemic Tianjin comparator. Several multi-center Chinese studies contrasting pre-pandemic (2018–2019) with post-pandemic (2023 onward) cohorts have reported a broadly consistent post-pandemic pattern: higher overall pathogen positivity and mixed-infection rates, a higher proportion of severe presentations, and shifts in the relative ranking, seasonal timing and age distribution of individual pathogens (Cui et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025). In Shanghai, post-pandemic test positivity rose markedly relative to 2019, with both RSV and ADV increasing and RSV’s onset shifting earlier into August, ahead of its conventional winter season (Liu et al., 2025); other Chinese cohorts spanning the pre-pandemic, pandemic and post-pandemic phases have likewise documented altered seasonal timing and age-distribution shifts for RSV, ADV and rhinovirus after non-pharmaceutical interventions were relaxed (Cui et al., 2024).Interpreted against this backdrop, our Tianjin observations show both continuities and departures. HRV’s endemic, weakly seasonal circulation—reflected in its leading position and broad March–December envelope—appears to have been less perturbed by the pandemic and its aftermath than that of the more strongly seasonal viruses. By contrast, the convergence of five of the six viruses onto a single sharp December peak is consistent with the compressed, intensified post-pandemic winter surge described elsewhere in China, plausibly reflecting the accumulated immunity debt from population-level exposure gaps in 2020–2022 (Cohen et al., 2021; Li et al., 2024) superimposed on the resumption of normal contact patterns. HBoV departed most sharply from this winter pattern, peaking instead in summer; to our knowledge, such an isolated warm-season peak has not been prominently reported as a post-pandemic phenomenon elsewhere in China. Whether it reflects a genuine post-pandemic shift in HBoV’s seasonal niche or a feature specific to Tianjin’s continental climate cannot be resolved with a single-center, single-period dataset, and we return to its biological and clinical significance in Section 4.4.4.3Climate-driven lagged effectsThe unadjusted and seasonally adjusted analyses answer different questions, and reading them together guards against a common pitfall in climate–infection studies. In the unadjusted analysis (Table 3), IFV appeared the most climate-responsive virus, with antecedent humidity and temperature aligning with later case counts, in keeping with the recognized seasonal phasing of influenza in temperate climates (Deyle et al., 2016; Kudo et al., 2019; Lowen et al., 2007; Lowen and Steel, 2014). Once seasonality and secular trend were held constant in the unified model, however, these IFV associations disappeared (Table 5). This does not mean that IFV has no climatic drivers. Rather, because ambient temperature and humidity in Tianjin themselves follow an almost perfect annual sinusoid, they are nearly collinear with the sine–cosine seasonal terms of the unified model; for a virus as tightly locked to the annual cycle as influenza (77.5% of deviance explained by season and trend alone), the model simply cannot separate the effect of “season” from that of “temperature” or “humidity.” The most that can be concluded is that, at the present monthly resolution, IFV shows no climatic association detectable independently of the seasonal cycle itself.The seasonally adjusted model instead isolated RSV and HMPV as the only viruses with climate associations independent of shared seasonality (Table 5): RSV tracked temperature and wind speed at short lags, while HMPV tracked temperature positively and humidity inversely, although its low case counts make these estimates imprecise and hypothesis-generating. HRV, ADV and HBoV showed no independent lagged signal, indicating that at monthly resolution their seasonal envelopes are not accompanied by a detectable climate effect beyond the annual cycle. This null result should not be read as evidence of climatic insensitivity. For these three viruses the seasonal-plus-trend baseline itself explained comparatively little of the monthly deviance (HRV 41.5%, HBoV 28.6%, ADV 17.1%; Table 4), so a large share of the variation in their case counts is left unaccounted for by season, trend and weather combined. Residual variation of that magnitude widens the standard errors, and with 36 monthly observations spanning three seasonal cycles only associations of substantial size could reach significance. A modest but real climate effect would probably have escaped detection here, and the finding is better described as uninformative for HRV, ADV and HBoV than as negative. The contrast between the two analyses carries the key methodological lesson: lagged climate associations in surveillance data can be interpreted only after seasonality has been accounted for.These post-pandemic patterns can be read against the pre-pandemic national baseline of Xu et al. (2021), who modelled a seven-virus panel—five of them shared with our own—across 81 sentinel hospitals in 22 Chinese provinces (2009–2013) and ranked the meteorological factors by climate region.
